definition_zh: 机会；可能性；偶然；碰巧；冒险
definition_en: an opportunity to do something; the possibility that something will happen; happening by luck
core_image: 掷出去还没落地的骰子，落点未定，一切皆有可能
scene: 班会选举时，老师鼓励每个同学都给自己一次上台展示的机会。 Take this chance to show your talents to the class.
sceneCN: 这里 chance 是「机会」（第 1 个义项：可以做某事的时机）；句意为抓住这次机会向全班展示才华。

derivatives.zh: 由 chance 加 -y 构成，义为「冒险的；不确定的」
由 chance 加 -ful 构成，义为「多变的；靠运气的」

senses.title: An opportunity to do something
senses.definition: a time when you can do something you want to do
senses.definitionCN: 能够做自己想做之事的时机
senses.example: Take this chance to show your talents to the class.
senses.exampleCN: 抓住这次机会向全班展示才华。
senses.why: What falls out is not planned; when events fall your way, that opening is your chance.
senses.whyCN: 掷出的点数并非计划所得；当事情恰好落在你这边，那个时机就是你的机会。

senses.title: The possibility that something will happen
senses.definition: how likely it is that something will happen
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能性大小
senses.example: There is a good chance of rain this afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 今天下午很可能下雨。
senses.why: The fall of the dice measures how likely a thing is, so the falling word names probability itself.
senses.whyCN: 骰子的点数可衡量一件事的倾向，掷落之词便转指可能性本身。

senses.title: Happening by luck, not plan
senses.definition: the way things happen without anyone planning them
senses.definitionCN: 事情在无人安排的情况下发生的方式
senses.example: I met my old friend quite by chance.
senses.exampleCN: 我偶遇了老朋友。
senses.why: What no one arranges belongs to the falling dice: unplanned events are pure chance.
senses.whyCN: 无人安排之事属于掷出的骰子：偶然发生之事就是纯然的 chance。

senses.title: To risk doing something
senses.definition: to risk doing something, hoping it will turn out well
senses.definitionCN: 冒险做某事，希望有好结果
senses.example: We will chance the weather and go cycling.
senses.exampleCN: 我们要赌一把天气，去骑自行车。
senses.why: Trusting to the fall of the dice becomes a verb of daring the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 把结果交给骰子的点数，便化作赌一把的动词。

intro.en: Chance comes from a Latin word for the fall of the dice, passing through French into English.
intro.cn: chance 源自拉丁语中指骰子掷落的词，经法语传入英语。

items.en: Late Latin cadentia meant a falling, built on cadere, to fall.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cadentia 指落下，源于动词 cadere（落下）。

items.en: Old French cheance meant the fall of dice and hence fortune.
items.cn: 古法语 cheance 指骰子的掷落，进而指运气。

items.en: Middle English chance kept the luck sense and grew the opportunity sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 chance 保留运气义，并发展出机会义。

items.en: The possibility sense spread into weather, games and everyday talk.
items.cn: 可能性之义渗入天气、游戏与日常会话。

items.en: Modern English uses chance for opportunity, probability, luck and risky trying.
items.cn: 现代英语的 chance 涵盖机会、可能性、运气与冒险一试。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects luck and opportunity words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收运气与机会类词。

entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改变」，拼写与 chance 仅差一字母。

entries.definition: To move the body to music.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「跳舞」，读音与 chance 词尾相近。

entries.definition: Risky and uncertain.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「冒险的」，由 chance 派生。

entries.definition: A chance to do something good.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「良机」，与 chance 的机会义相近。

entries.definition: Good or bad fortune that comes without planning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「运气」，与 chance 的偶然义相近。

entries.definition: The danger that something bad may happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风险」，与 chance 的冒险义相关。

normalIntro.en: Remember chance by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 chance。

normal.cn: chance 源自拉丁语 cadere（落下）。

normal.en: cadence, the rhythm of music, shares the same falling root.
normal.cn: cadence（节奏）与 chance 同享「落下」词根。

normal.en: by chance means without planning.
normal.cn: by chance 意为偶然、无意中。

normal.en: take a chance means to risk it.
normal.cn: take a chance 意为冒险一试。

normal.en: a slim chance means it is not likely.
normal.cn: a slim chance 意为希望渺茫。

abstract.en: Picture dice tumbling through the air before they land.
abstract.cn: 想象骰子落地前在空中翻滚。

abstract.en: Hear the soft clatter of dice on a wooden table.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见骰子落在木桌上的轻响。

abstract.en: Feel a door swinging open just as you reach it.
abstract.cn: 感受赶到时门恰好为你敞开的瞬间。

examples.cn: 抓住这次机会向全班展示才华。

examples.en: I met my old friend quite by chance.
examples.cn: 我纯属偶然遇到了老朋友。

examples.en: There is a good chance of rain this afternoon.
examples.cn: 今天下午很可能下雨。

intro.cn: chance 短小的词形里保留了拉丁语「落下」词根 cad-。

latinIntro.cn: 词根 cadere 还派生出 accident 与 cadence。

items.example: The police looked into the incident.

items.example: She read the poem with a lovely cadence.
Cycling there is chancy in winter.

definition_zh: 反射；反映；思考
definition_en: to throw back light, heat, or sound; to show or express something; to think carefully about
core_image: 静止的湖面把整排山影倒映出来
scene: 清晨湖面没有一丝风，对岸的山被完整地映在水里。 The still water reflected the whole line of hills.
sceneCN: 这里 reflected 是 reflect 的过去式，取「反射、映出」（第 1 个义项：把光或影像折回）；句意为静止的水面映出了整排山峦。画面里可留意：没有波纹的湖面、水中的山影。

derivatives.zh: 倒影；反映；沉思
反光的；沉思的
反光镜；反射器

senses.title: To throw back
senses.definition: to send back light, heat, or sound from a surface
senses.definitionCN: 从表面把光、热或声音送回去
senses.example: The still water reflected the whole line of hills.
senses.exampleCN: 静止的水面映出了整排山峦。
senses.why: The Latin verb is to bend back: a ray meets a surface and is bent away from it, as if the surface refused to keep it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「弯回去」：光线碰到表面后被折开，仿佛表面不肯留下它。

senses.title: To show or stand for
senses.definition: to show the nature or state of something
senses.definitionCN: 显示出某事物的性质或状况
senses.example: The report reflects the concerns of the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告反映了整个村子的关切。
senses.why: A surface that shows an image is a natural picture of a society that shows its own condition in its records.
senses.whyCN: 能映出影像的表面，自然成了「社会借记录显现自身状况」这一用法的比喻。

senses.title: To think carefully
senses.definition: to turn the mind back on an idea or an experience
senses.definitionCN: 把心思转回到某个想法或经历上
senses.example: She sat by the window and reflected on what he had said.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在窗边，思考他刚才说的话。
senses.why: Thinking is a bending back of attention: the mind leaves the outer scene and returns to what it already holds.
senses.whyCN: 思考是注意力的折返：心思离开外在景象，回到自己已经拥有的东西上。

intro.en: Reflect is to bend back; the word begins with light and ends with thought, and the path between them is a single metaphor.
intro.cn: reflect 意为「弯回去」；这个词从光开始，到思想结束，而两者之间的路径只是一个比喻。

items.en: Flectere meant to bend or curve, the base of a family of words about turning.
items.cn: flectere 意为弯曲，是表示「转向」的词族的词根。

items.en: Reflectere joined re-, back, with flectere and meant to bend or turn back.
items.cn: reflectere 由 re-（往回）与 flectere 组成，意为弯回去或转回去。

items.en: Natural philosophers used the word first for rays of light bent back from a surface.
items.cn: 自然哲学家最先用这个词指从表面折回的光线。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the same word described an image in a mirror and a mind turned back on itself.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，同一个词既指镜中的影像，也指回转自身的头脑。

items.en: The sense of showing a condition grew from the mirror: a record reflects what produced it.
items.cn: 「显现状况」这一义从镜子发展而来：一份记录会映出产生它的那个东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the Latin flectere; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of showing, mirroring, and thinking.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁 flectere 构成的动词；近义组收表示映现与思考的动词。

entries.definition: To turn something aside.
entries.definitionCN: 使偏斜；转移。

entries.definition: To change the pitch or form of a word.
entries.definitionCN: 屈折；变调。

entries.definition: An automatic response.
entries.definitionCN: 反射；本能反应。

entries.definition: To show an image of.

entries.definition: To make visible or evident.

entries.definition: To think over carefully.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细考虑。

entries.definition: To think about before deciding.
entries.definitionCN: 考虑；斟酌。

normalIntro.en: The word is a bending back, whether of light from water or of attention from the world to the self.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「弯回去」，既可以是水面对光的折返，也可以是注意力从外界折回自身。

normal.en: Re plus flectere, back plus bend: light bends back from the water.
normal.cn: re 加 flectere，往回加弯：光从水面弯回来。

normal.en: A mirror reflects your face; a report reflects the facts.
normal.cn: 镜子映出你的脸，报告映出事实。

normal.en: Reflect on a question means to bend your mind back to it.
normal.cn: reflect on a question 指把心思折回到这个问题上。

normal.en: Reflective people think; reflective surfaces shine.
normal.cn: reflective 的人爱思考，reflective 的表面会反光。

normal.en: Do not confuse reflect with deflect, which turns things aside.
normal.cn: 别把 reflect 与 deflect 弄混，后者是把东西拨到一边。

abstract.en: To reflect is to let what is outside pass through you and come back changed.
abstract.cn: 反射，就是让外界之物穿过你，再以改变过的样子回来。

abstract.en: A society is known by what it chooses to reflect on.
abstract.cn: 一个社会因它选择反思什么而为人所知。

abstract.en: The mirror and the mind use the same verb because both return an image.
abstract.cn: 镜子与头脑共用同一个动词，因为两者都送回一个影像。

examples.en: The still water reflected the whole line of hills.
examples.cn: 静止的水面映出了整排山峦。

examples.en: The report reflects the concerns of the whole village.
examples.cn: 这份报告反映了整个村子的关切。

examples.en: She sat by the window and reflected on what he had said.
examples.cn: 她坐在窗边，思考他刚才说的话。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 flect（弯）：光弯回来是反射，事实弯回来是反映，心思弯回来是思考。

root: 拉丁 flectere（弯曲）→ reflectere（弯回去）→ 英语 reflect；同族有 reflection、reflective、reflector，形近的 deflect、inflect、reflex 共用 flectere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is bending back; the senses move from a ray returned by a surface, to a record showing its source, to a mind turned back on itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「弯回去」；义项从表面送回的光线，到映出其来源的记录，再到回转自身的头脑。

intro.en: A Latin verb of bending takes a prefix of return, and the compound passes from rays of light to the movement of thought.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「弯曲」动词接上表返回的前缀，这个复合词便从光线走到了思想的运动。

latinIntro.en: The base is flectere, to bend, with re- meaning back; the participle reflexus feeds the noun.

definition_zh: 经验；经历；体验；感受（名词）；经历；体验（动词）
definition_en: knowledge or skill gained from doing something, an event that affects you, or the feeling it produces
core_image: 走过一遍的路留下脚印：事情发生后，它就存进了你这个人里
scene: 第一次独自坐火车去外婆家的孩子，下车时攥着车票回头看了看，妈妈说： This trip will be a valuable experience for you.
sceneCN: 这里 experience 指「一次有影响的经历」（第 2 个义项：亲历的事件）；句意为这次独自出行对你很有价值。

derivatives.zh: 有经验的；老练的（过去分词作形容词，义为「已被经历打磨过的」）
缺乏经验的（in- 加 experienced，义为「还没被事情打磨过」）
实验（同源近亲，义为「主动制造一次经历来试」）
经验主义的（同根异形，义为「以经历为依据的」）

senses.title: Knowledge gained by doing
senses.definition: the knowledge or skill that comes from actually doing or seeing something
senses.definitionCN: 从实际做或亲眼见中得来的知识与技能
senses.example: She has five years of teaching experience.
senses.exampleCN: 她有五年教学经验。
senses.why: The root is to try out through the body: what passes through you stays as know-how.
senses.whyCN: 词根是用身体去尝试：从你身上经过的东西会沉淀为本领。

senses.title: An event that happens to you
senses.definition: something that happens to you and leaves an effect
senses.definitionCN: 发生在你身上并留下影响的事
senses.example: This trip will be a valuable experience for you.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行对你将是一次宝贵的经历。
senses.why: The same passing-through, seen as one complete event rather than accumulated skill.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「经过」，这次被看作一个完整事件，而非积累的本领。

senses.title: The inner feeling of undergoing something
senses.definition: the conscious feeling produced by undergoing something
senses.definitionCN: 亲身经历某事时产生的内在感受
senses.example: Pain is a bitter experience no one enjoys.
senses.exampleCN: 疼痛是一种没人喜欢的痛苦体验。
senses.why: The path runs inside now: what passes through you is felt, not stored as skill.
senses.whyCN: 路线转入内在：经过你的是感受，而不是沉淀为技能的东西。

senses.title: To undergo or live through something
senses.definition: to meet with or live through something as it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在某事发生时遭遇或经受它
senses.example: The city experienced its worst storm in decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市经历了数十年来最严重的风暴。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: the person is now the road that events travel on.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词：人变成了事件驶过的那条路。

intro.en: Experience comes from Latin experiri, "to try out", through French, and keeps the sense of testing by living through it.
intro.cn: experience 源自拉丁语 experiri「尝试」，经法语进入英语，保留了「亲身经过来验证」的意思。

items.en: Latin experiri meant "to try, to test", from ex- (out of) + peritus (tested, skilled).
items.cn: 拉丁语 experiri 意为「尝试、检验」，由 ex-（从…出来）+ peritus（受试的、熟练的）构成。

items.en: The root per- carries the idea of risk: to try is to put yourself on the line.
items.cn: 词根 per- 带有「冒险」的意味：尝试就是把自己押上去。

items.en: Old French experience carried both the trying and the knowledge it yields.
items.cn: 古法语 experience 兼指尝试与尝试所得的知识。

items.en: Middle English borrowed it in the fourteenth century for tested knowledge and lived events.
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语借入，兼指经过验证的知识与亲历的事件。

items.en: Modern English widened it to inner feeling and to the verb of undergoing events.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到内在感受，并用作「经历某事」的动词。

note.en: These neighbours share the per- root or the idea of living through something.
note.cn: 下列词与 experience 同根，或同样有「亲身经过」的意思。

entries.definition: a planned test made on purpose
entries.definitionCN: 实验（同根，主动制造的经历）

entries.definition: one made skilled by testing
entries.definitionCN: 专家（同根，被试炼出来的人）

entries.definitionCN: 经验主义的（同根异形）

entries.definition: related to an empire
entries.definitionCN: 帝国的（拼写相近，词源不同，来自 imperare「命令」）

entries.definition: what is known
entries.definitionCN: 知识（不强调亲身经过）

entries.definition: a meeting or event faced
entries.definitionCN: 遭遇；际遇（事件义近）

entries.definition: an exciting risky experience
entries.definitionCN: 冒险经历（ excitement 更强）

normalIntro.en: Five associations from the real root and usage.
normalIntro.cn: 五条来自真实词根与用法的联想。

normal.en: ex- (out) + per- (try, risk): you send yourself out to be tested.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex-（向外）+ 词根 per-（尝试、冒险）：把自己派出去受试。

normal.en: Experiment is the same root making a test on purpose.
normal.cn: experiment 是同根词，故意制造一次测试。

normal.en: Expert is what testing makes of you.
normal.cn: expert 是被试炼打造出来的你。

normal.en: Experienced vs inexperienced: polished or not yet polished.
normal.cn: experienced 与 inexperienced：被打磨过与否。

normal.en: Learn from experience means the road itself was the teacher.
normal.cn: learn from experience 意思是这条路本身就是老师。

abstract.en: Picture footprints on a path: each event leaves a mark inside you.
abstract.cn: 想象路上的脚印：每件事都在你心里留下印记。

abstract.en: Skills are old footprints you can walk again; events are single big marks.
abstract.cn: 技能是可以重走的旧脚印，事件是一次性的大印记。

abstract.en: To experience is to be the road itself while events drive over.
abstract.cn: to experience 就是当事件驶过时，自己成为那条路。

examples.en: This trip will be a valuable experience for you.
examples.cn: 这次旅行对你将是一次宝贵的经历。

examples.en: She has five years of teaching experience.
examples.cn: 她有五年教学经验。

examples.en: The city experienced its worst storm in decades.
examples.cn: 这座城市经历了数十年来最严重的风暴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗死匹日恩死」——一颗死磕的匹夫每日经历磨炼，终成老手。

root: 源自拉丁语 experiri「尝试、检验」，由 ex-（向外）+ peritus「受试的、熟练的」构成，词根 per- 含冒险义；与 experiment、expert 同根。经古法语于十四世纪进入中古英语。

sensesIntro.en: From being tested by trying, the word covers gained skill, single events, inner feeling, and undergoing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「尝试中受检验」出发，覆盖所得本领、单个事件、内在感受与「经历」这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footprints left on the road you have walked
core.cn: 核心意象：走过的路上留下的脚印

definition_zh: 位置；方位；姿势；职位；立场；处境；安置；使处于
definition_en: the place where someone or something is, the way the body is arranged, a job, an opinion on an issue, a situation, or to put something in a particular place
core_image: 棋盘上一枚棋子被手指捏起，轻轻放进一个新的格子
scene: 比赛暂停时，教练把几枚棋子从棋盘边角挪到中央，又退后看了看。 He moved the knight into a stronger position on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 position 是「位置」（第 1 个义项：某物所在的地方）；句意为他把马挪到棋盘上更有利的位置。图中可辨识物件：棋盘、棋子、教练。

pos.zh: 位置；方位；姿势；职位；立场；处境

derivatives.zh: 由 position 加 -al 构成，义为「位置的；与位置有关的」
由 position 加 -ing 构成，义为「定位；摆放」
由 position 加 -er 构成，义为「定位器；定位装置」

senses.title: The place where something is
senses.definition: the exact place where a person or thing is or should be
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物所在或应在的确切地点
senses.example: The map marks the position of every well in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地图标出了山谷里每一口井的位置。
senses.why: Latin ponere means to place, and positio is a placing; the first sense is the result of that act, the spot where something has been put.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ponere 意为放置，positio 是「放置」这一动作；第一个义项就是动作的结果——某物被放定的那个点。

senses.title: The way the body is held
senses.definition: the way someone stands, sits or holds the body
senses.definitionCN: 人站立、坐着或摆放身体的方式
senses.example: Sit in a comfortable position with your back straight.
senses.exampleCN: 挺直背，以一种舒服的姿势坐好。
senses.why: A body placed this way or that forms a visible arrangement, so the placing word comes to name the shape the body makes.
senses.whyCN: 身体这样摆或那样摆，会形成看得见的安排；于是「放置」这个词开始指身体摆出的形状。

senses.title: A job or official role
senses.definition: a job in an organization, or the rank someone holds
senses.definitionCN: 在一个组织中的工作，或某人所居的级别
senses.example: She applied for a position in the research department.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了研究部的一个职位。
senses.why: A post is a place in an ordered structure: the person is placed in it, and the word for the placing becomes the word for the slot.
senses.whyCN: 职位是有序结构中的一个位置：人被放进这个位置，于是表示「放置」的词变成了表示「位置、空缺」的词。

senses.title: An opinion on an issue
senses.definition: the opinion someone takes on a question, especially one they are prepared to defend
senses.definitionCN: 某人对某个问题所持的看法，尤指愿意为之辩护的看法
senses.example: The committee took a firm position against the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会坚决反对修建这条新路。
senses.why: A standpoint is a place one stands; taking a position is choosing where to stand in an argument, so spatial placing turns into opinion.
senses.whyCN: 立场就是站的地方；表明立场就是在争论中选定站处，于是空间上的「放置」变成了看法。

senses.title: To put something in place
senses.definition: to put someone or something in a particular place or arrangement, often carefully
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物放到特定地点或安排中，往往带有仔细的意味
senses.example: He positioned the lamp so that the light fell on the page.
senses.exampleCN: 他把灯安置好，让光落在书页上。
senses.why: The noun names the resulting place; the verb is the act of producing it, and English formed the verb from the noun in modern times.
senses.whyCN: 名词指放置之后形成的位置；动词则是产生这个位置的动作，英语到近代才由名词造出这个动词。

intro.en: Position is the Latin verb ponere, to place, turned into a noun through its participle positus; English took it from French and later made a verb of it again.
intro.cn: position 是拉丁动词 ponere（放置）经其过去分词 positus 变成的名词；英语从法语借入，后来又把名词重新做成动词。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and its past participle positus meant placed or set.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、安放，它的过去分词 positus 意为被放置的。

items.en: Positio was the abstract noun for a placing, and it could already mean the place a thing occupied.
items.cn: positio 是表示「放置」的抽象名词，当时已经可以指某物占据的位置。

items.en: Old French passed position to English in the fourteenth century as a word for a place or an arrangement.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把 position 传给英语，指位置或安排方式。

items.en: The word gained the senses of a military post, a job and a stated opinion, all built on the idea of a place one occupies.
items.cn: 这个词陆续获得军事据点、职位与明确看法等义项，全部建立在「所占之处」这一想法上。

items.en: Modern English formed the verb to position and added phrases such as market position, keeping the old placing core.
items.cn: 现代英语造出动词 to position，并添上 market position 一类说法，保留的仍是古老的「放置」核心。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb ponere; the near-meaning group gathers words for place, stance and job.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁动词 ponere 构成的词；近义组收表示地点、立场与职位的词。

entries.definition: Relating to position or place.
entries.definitionCN: 由 position 加 -al 构成，义为「位置的；与位置有关的」。

entries.definition: From Latin positivus and positus; it first meant placed or fixed, and now means affirmative.
entries.definitionCN: 与 positus 同根，原指被放置、被定下的，现代义为「肯定的」。

entries.definition: To put together, from com- plus ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-（一起）与 ponere（放置）构成，义为「组成；创作」。

entries.definition: To put down, from de- plus ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de-（向下）与 ponere（放置）构成，义为「存放；沉积」。

entries.definition: The place where something is.
entries.definitionCN: 位置；地点；强调地理上的所在，不指姿势或立场。

entries.definition: A public attitude towards an issue, or the way the body stands.
entries.definitionCN: 立场；站姿；同时覆盖态度与身体姿态。

entries.definition: A job or a place where someone is stationed.
entries.definitionCN: 职位；岗位；强调被派驻的工作地点。

entries.definition: The act of putting something in a place, or a job arranged for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 安置；安排；强调安排的动作或实习岗位。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on the Latin verb for placing, and its family keeps returning to spots, postures, posts and stands.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词立足于拉丁语表示「放置」的动词，同族词反复回到地点、姿势、职位与立场。

normal.en: Ponere means to place, and its participle positus is the stem behind position, positive and posit.
normal.cn: ponere 意为放置，它的过去分词 positus 正是 position、positive 与 posit 共同的词干。

normal.en: Compose is com- plus ponere, to put together; deposit is de- plus ponere, to put down.
normal.cn: compose 是 com- 加 ponere，意为放在一起；deposit 是 de- 加 ponere，意为放下。

normal.en: Positional adds -al and simply describes anything about place or arrangement.
normal.cn: positional 加 -al，只用来描述与位置或安排有关的事物。

normal.en: A job is a position because a person is placed into a slot in an organization.
normal.cn: 职位之所以叫 position，是因为人被放进组织中的一个格子里。

normal.en: A position in an argument is a place to stand, which is why one word covers location and opinion.
normal.cn: 争论中的立场就是站的地方，所以一个词同时覆盖位置与看法。

abstract.en: A position is where you are, but also where you choose to stand, and English lets one word hold both.
abstract.cn: 位置既是你所在之处，也是你选择站立之处，英语让一个词同时装下两者。

abstract.en: On a board every piece has a position, and changing it changes what the piece can do.
abstract.cn: 棋盘上每枚棋子都有位置，改变位置就改变了它所能做的事。

abstract.en: To be in position is to be ready, which is why the word appears in sports, jobs and arguments alike.
abstract.cn: 就位就是准备好了，所以这个词在体育、职场与争论里都会出现。

examples.en: He moved the knight into a stronger position on the board.
examples.cn: 他把马挪到棋盘上更有利的位置。

examples.en: She applied for a position in the research department.
examples.cn: 她申请了研究部的一个职位。

examples.en: The committee took a firm position against the new road.
examples.cn: 委员会坚决反对修建这条新路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡贼神」——把棋子摆到棋盘上的某一点，那个点就定了；position 就是位置，也是职位与立场。

root: 源自拉丁 ponere（放置）的过去分词 positus，再由抽象名词 positio 经古法语进入英语；同族词有 compose、deposit、positive。注意与来自 portare（搬运）的 port、portable 区分：position 的核心是「放」，不是「搬」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place something occupies; the senses branch into physical location, body posture, a job slot, a standpoint, and the act of placing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是某物所占据的地方；义项由此分出物理位置、身体姿势、职位空缺、立场，以及放置的动作。

core.cn: 核心意象：棋盘上一枚棋子被手指捏起，轻轻放进一个新的格子。

branches.en: a marker pinned to a spot on a map
branches.cn: 钉在地图某点上的标记

branches.en: a back held straight in a chair
a name written into an empty slot on an org chart
branches.cn: 组织架构图空格里写下的名字

branches.en: a delegate standing to state a view
a camera positioned to catch the whole stage
branches.cn: 被安放好以拍到整个舞台的相机

latinIntro.en: Position comes from Latin ponere, to place, through its participle positus and the noun positio; the same verb also gives compose and deposit.

definition_zh: 车库；汽车修理厂；（美）车库 sale 式的旧货市集
definition_en: a building where a car is kept or repaired
core_image: 卷帘门升起，车灯照亮一车库的工具与油味
scene: 傍晚，爸爸掀开防水布检查轮胎。 The car hid in the garage from the sudden summer rain.
sceneCN: 这里 garage 是「车库」（第 1 个义项：存放汽车的建筑）；句意为骤雨突至，汽车躲进了车库。

derivatives.zh: 动词 garaged 的分词形容词用法，义为「存放在车库里的」
动名词形式，义为「车辆入库存放」

senses.title: A building for keeping a car
senses.definition: a shelter or building where a car or vehicle is stored
senses.definitionCN: 存放汽车等车辆的建筑或棚屋
senses.example: The ladder lives in the garage next to the bicycle.
senses.exampleCN: 梯子放在车库里的自行车旁边。
senses.why: The word first named the safe shelter of a vehicle, so the storage image is the base.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先指车辆的安全庇护所，存放画面是基础。

senses.title: A workshop for vehicle repair
senses.definition: a business place where vehicles are repaired or serviced
senses.definitionCN: 修理或保养车辆的营业场所
senses.example: The mechanic at the garage checked the brakes.
senses.exampleCN: 修车厂的技师检查了刹车。
senses.why: A shelter that keeps cars invites keeping them healthy, so repair grew on the same spot.
senses.whyCN: 存放车辆的地方自然延伸为养护车辆，修理义在同一地点生长。

senses.title: Fuel and service station
senses.definition: a roadside place selling petrol and small repairs, chiefly British
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中路旁售油兼小修的场所
senses.example: They stopped at the garage to fill the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在加油站停车加油。
senses.why: One roof once covered petrol pumps, tyres, and tools, so the name covered the forecourt too.
senses.whyCN: 一个屋顶曾同时罩住油泵、轮胎与工具，于是名称也覆盖了整个场院。

senses.title: To park in a shelter
senses.definition: to put or keep a vehicle in a garage
senses.definitionCN: 把车辆放入车库保管
senses.example: Remember to garage the scooter before the frost.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻前记得把小摩托收进车库。
senses.why: Buildings act, in English habit, so the place lent itself to a verb.
senses.whyCN: 英语习惯让建筑「行动」，于是场所名转为动词。

senses.title: Humble home-made origin
senses.definition: started in a home garage, describing famous low-budget beginnings
senses.definitionCN: 形容从自家车库起步的知名创业或乐队
senses.example: The company tells a garage start-up story.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司讲述着车库创业的故事。
senses.why: The garage is the least expensive room with a lock, so dreams started there and the label stuck.
senses.whyCN: 车库是最便宜的有锁空间，梦想从那里起步，标签随之定型。

intro.en: Garage is French in origin, built on a word for shelter or protection.
intro.cn: garage 源于法语，建立在表示庇护、防护的词上。

items.en: French garer meant to shelter, to dock, or to protect.
items.cn: 法语 garer 意为庇护、停靠、防护。

items.en: Garer itself is generally traced to a Germanic root meaning to guard or watch.
items.cn: garer 一般认为源自意为看守、警戒的日耳曼词根。

items.en: French garage formed as the place where vehicles were garées.
items.cn: 法语 garage 由「被庇护之所」构成车辆存放地。

items.en: English borrowed garage around the first automobile age, about one century ago.
items.cn: 英语在汽车时代之初，约一个世纪前借入 garage。

items.en: Modern English extended it to repairs, petrol, verbs, and start-up legends.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到维修、加油、动词用法与创业传奇。

note.en: Garage carries two British pronunciations and hides near-neighbours like garbage.
note.cn: garage 在英式英语中读音分裂，拼写上还紧邻 garbage。

entries.definition: a room for making or repairing

abstract.en: See the roller door rise and headlight beams sweep the tools.
abstract.cn: 看卷帘门升起，车灯扫过一排排工具。

abstract.en: Hear the French tail -age, soft as engine idle.
abstract.cn: 法语词尾 -age 读起来像发动机的怠速声。

abstract.en: Picture two famous companies born where a lawnmower once parked.
abstract.cn: 想象两家著名公司诞生在从前停割草机的地方。

examples.en: He converted the garage into a small workshop.
examples.cn: 他把车库改成了小工坊。

examples.en: The garage replaced the gearbox in one afternoon.
examples.cn: 修车厂一下午就换好了变速箱。

examples.en: Remember to garage the bicycle tonight.

sensesIntro.en: Vehicle shelter is the base; repair shops, petrol stops, the verb, and start-up lore all grew around it.
sensesIntro.cn: 车辆庇护所是基础；修车厂、加油站、动词用法与创业传说都围绕它生长。

items.exampleCN: 法语至今仍说把车停进院子。

definition_zh: 欺骗；作弊；骗取；骗子
definition_en: to act dishonestly to win or gain something; a dishonest person
core_image: 把袖子里藏的另一张牌悄悄换出来
scene: 同桌考试时偷偷瞟我的卷子，被老师发现了。 He tried to cheat in the exam by looking at my paper.
sceneCN: 这里 cheat 是「作弊」（第 1 个义项：不诚实地取利）；句意是他想偷看我的卷子作弊，被老师发现。

derivatives.zh: 由 cheat 加 -er 构成，义为「骗子；作弊者」
由 cheat 加 -ing 构成，义为「作弊；欺骗行为」
由 cheat 加 sheet 构成，义为「小抄」

senses.title: To break rules secretly to win
senses.definition: to act against rules in a game, exam or sport without being seen
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、考试或运动中暗中违反规则
senses.example: He cheated by hiding notes in his sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 他把小抄藏在袖子里作弊。
senses.why: Winning unfairly needs hiding, like a card swapped from a sleeve.
senses.whyCN: 不公平地赢需要遮掩，就像从袖子里换牌。

senses.title: To trick someone for gain
senses.definition: to make someone believe something false so you gain
senses.definitionCN: 使某人信假话以从中获利
senses.example: A stranger cheated my grandmother out of two hundred yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 一个陌生人骗了我奶奶两百元。
senses.why: The trick pulls money or trust out of another's pocket.
senses.whyCN: 花招从别人的口袋里掏走钱或信任。

senses.title: A dishonest person or act
senses.definition: a person who cheats, or the act itself
senses.definitionCN: 行骗的人或行为本身
senses.example: Nobody wants to play cards with a cheat.
senses.exampleCN: 没人愿意和骗子打牌。
senses.why: The doer and the deed share one short word.
senses.whyCN: 做坏事的人和坏事共用这个短词。

intro.en: Cheat grew out of the word escheat, a lawyer's term.
intro.cn: cheat 由法律术语 escheat 蜕变而来。

items.en: Old French escheat meant property that falls to the lord when its owner dies without heirs.
items.cn: 古法语 escheat 指无人继承时归于领主的财产。

items.en: English borrowed escheat for the same legal meaning.
items.cn: 英语借入 escheat 表示同样的法律意义。

items.en: Lawyers shortened the noun to cheat.
items.cn: 法律界人士把该名词缩略为 cheat。

items.en: Cheat then meant the fraudulent getting of another's property.
items.cn: cheat 随后指用欺诈手段夺取他人财产。

items.en: The verb widened to cheating in games, love and study.
items.cn: 动词用法扩展到游戏、感情和学习中的欺骗。

note.en: Close spellings and close meanings of dishonesty.
note.cn: 与「不诚实」形近义近的词。

entries.definition: costing little; one letter apart
entries.definitionCN: 便宜的（形近词）

entries.definition: a baby bird's sound; same sound
entries.definitionCN: （雏鸟）吱吱声（同音词）

entries.definition: a person who cheats
entries.definitionCN: 作弊者

entries.definition: a sheet of information; letters close, no relation
entries.definitionCN: 图表（形近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to make someone believe what is false
entries.definitionCN: 欺骗

entries.definition: to fool someone, often less seriously
entries.definitionCN: 哄骗

entries.definition: serious dishonest gain, often legal word
entries.definitionCN: 欺诈（常为法律用语）

entries.definition: truthful and fair
entries.definitionCN: 诚实的

normalIntro.en: One short word hiding a dishonest act.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词里藏着不光彩的行为。

normal.en: cheat means to win by breaking rules.
normal.cn: cheat 指靠违规取胜。

normal.en: cheat in an exam is copying or hiding notes.
normal.cn: 考试作弊就是抄袭或藏小抄。

normal.en: cheat somebody out of money takes money by tricks.
normal.cn: cheat somebody out of money 用花招骗钱。

normal.en: a cheat is the dishonest person.
normal.cn: a cheat 指骗子。

normal.en: cheat sounds like cheap with a t.
normal.cn: cheat 听起来像 cheap 换了个 t。

abstract.en: Picture extra cards slipping out of a card player's sleeve.
abstract.cn: 想象牌桌旁从袖口滑出的多余牌。

abstract.en: Picture a student's eyes sliding sideways toward another's paper.
abstract.cn: 想象学生的视线偷偷滑向别人的卷子。

abstract.en: Picture a false coin glittering in a market hand.
abstract.cn: 想象市场里一只手闪烁着假硬币。

examples.en: She refused to cheat even when the test was hard.
examples.cn: 即使考试很难，她也拒绝作弊。

examples.en: The old man was cheated by a fake phone call.
examples.cn: 老人被一通假电话骗了。

examples.en: Cheats never win real respect.
examples.cn: 骗子永远赢不来真正的尊重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欺特」——他专门欺负特别信任他的人，用花招骗人，所以「欺特」= cheat。

root: 古法语 escheat（无主财产归领主）→ 中古英语 escheat 缩略为 cheat（欺诈取得）→ 动词、名词。与 escheat 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Secret rule-breaking, tricking for gain, and the dishonest person.
sensesIntro.cn: 暗中违规、骗取利益与行骗之人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: winning with a hidden false card
core.cn: 核心意象：用暗藏的假牌取胜

branches.en: Breaking rules in tests and games
Tricking people out of money
The person and the act
Trust that gets broken
Fairness lost in play

intro.en: Cheat works alone and inside honest-family opposites.
intro.cn: cheat 可独立使用，也可与反义词族对照。

latinIntro.en: The source is Old French law, not Latin stems.
latinIntro.cn: 源头是古法语法律用语，而非拉丁词干。

items.example: The cheater lost all his friends.
items.exampleCN: 那个骗子失去了所有朋友。

items.example: Cheating is punished in our school.
items.exampleCN: 我们学校对作弊有处罚。

items.example: The teacher found his cheat sheet.
A dishonest player spoils the game.
items.exampleCN: 不诚实的玩家毁掉比赛。

items.example: He tricked me with a false story.

latinEntries.meaning: to fall away, source of escheat
latinEntries.meaningCN: 落出、脱落（escheat 的拉丁源头）

definition_zh: 铁路（英式）；铁路系统；铁路运输
definition_en: a track of rails with stations and signals, the usual British word for a railroad; the organization and system that runs trains; transport by train
core_image: 山谷里一座长满草旧车站，月台尽头立着褪色站牌
scene: 山谷里的旧车站已经长满草，月台尽头还立着一块褪色的站牌。 The old railway once carried timber down the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 railway 是「铁路（英式说法）」（第 1 个义项：带车站与信号系统的轨道线路）；句意为这条旧铁路曾把木料运下山谷。画面里可留意：长草的月台、褪色站牌、通向谷底的轨线。

pos.zh: 铁路（英式）；铁路系统；铁路运输

derivatives.zh: railway 的第一成分，指单根轨条
美式对应词，指铁路或铁路公司
railway 与 man 复合，指铁路员工

senses.title: A track with stations and signals
senses.definition: a line of rails with its stations, signals and equipment, the usual British word for a railroad
senses.definitionCN: 带车站、信号与设备的轨道线路，英式英语对铁路的常用说法
senses.example: The old railway closed in the nineteen sixties.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧铁路在二十世纪六十年代停运了。
senses.why: British English joined rail and way to name the whole line, while American English chose rail and road.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语把 rail 与 way 组合起来命名整条线路，而美式英语选择了 rail 与 road。

senses.title: The organization and system
senses.definition: the body that owns the line and runs the trains
senses.definitionCN: 拥有线路并经营列车的机构
senses.example: She works for the national railway.
senses.exampleCN: 她在国家铁路部门工作。
senses.why: As with many networks, the physical line and the institution that operates it are called by one name.
senses.whyCN: 和许多网络一样，实体线路与运营它的机构共用一个名字。

senses.title: Transport by train
senses.definition: the carrying of people or goods by train, considered as a mode of transport
senses.definitionCN: 以火车运送人或货物，作为一种运输方式
senses.example: Goods moved by railway until the road was widened.
senses.exampleCN: 在公路拓宽之前，货物靠铁路运输。
senses.why: The system's name also names the service it provides, which is why people speak of sending something by railway.
senses.whyCN: 系统的名字也指它提供的服务，所以人们会说用铁路运送某物。

intro.en: Railway is a nineteenth-century English compound of rail and way, coined in Britain to name the new lines of track.
intro.cn: railway 是十九世纪的英语复合词，由 rail 与 way 组成，在英国被造出来命名新兴的轨道线路。

items.en: Rail came from the Latin word for a straight rule through French, and named the metal bar itself.
items.cn: rail 经法语来自拉丁语表示直尺的词，指的就是那根金属条。

items.en: Way is a native English word for a path or a route, older than any railway.
items.cn: way 是英语本族词，指路径或路线，比任何铁路都古老。

items.en: The compound railway named the way made of rails, a route built for locomotives.
items.cn: 复合词 railway 指由轨条铺成的路，为机车修建的路线。

items.en: British English kept railway for the line and the system, while American English settled on railroad.
items.cn: 英式英语保留 railway 指线路与系统，美式英语则固定用 railroad。

items.en: Modern English uses railway for the track, the company and the transport service, especially outside North America.
items.cn: 现代英语用 railway 指轨道、公司与运输服务，尤其在北美以外。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same compound; the near-meaning group gathers words for rail systems and routes.
note.cn: 形近组收同一复合词的形式；近义组收表示铁路系统与路线的词。

entries.definition: The American word for the same system.
entries.definitionCN: 同一系统的美式说法。

entries.definition: A single metal bar for wheels.
entries.definitionCN: 供车轮行驶的一根金属条。

entries.definition: A person employed by a railway.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇于铁路的人。

entries.definition: A single route of track between places.
entries.definitionCN: 两地之间的一条轨道线路。

entries.definition: A route of track or wire between places.
entries.definitionCN: 两地之间的轨道或线路。

entries.definition: The pair of rails a train runs on.
entries.definitionCN: 火车行驶其上的那对钢轨。

entries.definition: A set of connected routes.
entries.definitionCN: 相互连接的路线集合。

entries.definition: The carrying of people or goods.
entries.definitionCN: 人或货物的运送。

normalIntro.en: The word is rail plus way, the British way of naming a road of rails; the American cousin is railroad.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 rail 加 way，是英式命名「轨条之路」的方式；它的美国亲戚是 railroad。

normal.en: Railway is rail plus way, railroad is rail plus road: two languages, one idea.
normal.cn: railway 是 rail 加 way，railroad 是 rail 加 road：两种语言，同一个想法。

normal.en: A railway station is where the line meets the town, and a railway carriage is one coach on it.
normal.cn: railway station 是线路与城镇相接之处，railway carriage 是线上的一节车厢。

normal.en: The national railway is the publicly owned system, as opposed to a private company.
normal.cn: the national railway 指公有的铁路系统，与私营公司相对。

normal.en: By railway is less common than by rail, which is the usual short phrase.
normal.cn: by railway 不如 by rail 常用，后者才是通常的简短说法。

normal.en: A railwayman works on the line, a word that survives mainly in British writing.
normal.cn: railwayman 指在铁路上工作的人，这个词主要保留在英式书面语里。

abstract.en: A railway is a promise that the same route will be there tomorrow, which is why it changed how people planned their lives.
abstract.cn: 铁路是一种承诺：同一条路线明天仍在那里，因此它改变了人们安排生活的方式。

abstract.en: Cutting a railway through a valley is an act that both connects and divides the land.
abstract.cn: 在山谷里修一条铁路，既连接也分割了这片土地。

abstract.en: When a railway closes, the towns along it quietly become places people pass by instead of stop at.
abstract.cn: 一条铁路停运后，沿线的城镇悄然变成人们经过而不再停留的地方。

examples.en: The railway between the two towns was built in eighteen fifty.
examples.cn: 两镇之间的铁路建于1850年。

examples.en: He found work on the railway after the mill closed.
examples.cn: 磨坊关闭后，他在铁路部门找到了工作。

examples.en: Timber was carried by railway until the road was improved.
examples.cn: 在公路改善之前，木料靠铁路运输。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐欧威」——轨条铺成一条路，向远方延伸，记住 railway 是铁路。

root: rail（轨条，源自拉丁语 regula）+ way（路，英语本族词）复合而成，十九世纪出现；同族有 railroad、railwayman。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a way of rails; the senses divide into the British railway line, the system that runs it, and transport by train.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「由轨条铺成的路」；义项分为英式铁路线路、运营它的系统，以及铁路运输。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an overgrown station in a valley, a faded sign at the platform's end.
core.cn: 核心意象：山谷里长满草的旧车站，月台尽头一块褪色的站牌。

branches.en: a track disappearing into a valley
a timetable in a station office
branches.cn: 车站办公室里的时刻表

branches.en: timber stacked on a flat wagon
rails rusting under long grass
the same line, once busy and once abandoned
branches.cn: 同一条线路，一次繁忙，一次废弃

intro.en: The compound joins a Latin-derived rail to a native way, and English endings extend it to workers and to individual lines.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把源自拉丁语的 rail 与本族的 way 结合，英语词尾又把它扩展到工作者与单条线路。

latinIntro.en: Only rail has a Latin source, the word for a straight rule.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 rail 有拉丁语来源，即表示直尺的词。

items.meaning: a stopping place on a line

definition_zh: 温和的；轻柔的；出身高贵的；驯服的
definition_en: kind, mild, and careful, or belonging to a family of high social standing
core_image: 一只手轻轻托起受伤的小鸟，怕惊扰了它
scene: 雨停了，屋檐还在滴水。 A gentle breeze dried the washing without knocking it down.
sceneCN: 这里 gentle 是「轻柔的」（第 2 个义项：力量不猛烈）；句意为一阵轻柔的微风晾干了衣物，却没把它吹落。

pos.zh: 温和的；轻柔的；出身高贵的

derivatives.zh: gentle 加 -ly 构成，义为「轻柔地；温和地」
gentle 加 -ness 构成，义为「温和；温文」
gentle + man 构成，义为「绅士；先生」

senses.title: Kind and considerate in manner
senses.definition: kind and careful not to hurt or upset others
senses.definitionCN: 和善且小心不伤害或冒犯他人
senses.example: The nurse spoke in a gentle voice to the old man.
senses.exampleCN: 护士用温柔的声音对老人说话。
senses.why: High-born people were expected to be well-mannered, so refined behaviour became the human sense.
senses.whyCN: 出身高贵者被期待举止有教养，于是「有教养的举止」成为关于人的核心义。

senses.title: Not forceful or strong
senses.definition: mild in force, movement, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 力量、运动或程度上的轻微不猛烈
senses.example: She gave the rope a gentle pull.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻拉了一下绳子。
senses.why: The refined touch of a trained hand transfers to any mild force, wind, slope, or soap.
senses.whyCN: 受训之手的文雅触碰转移到一切轻微力量上，如微风、缓坡、温和的肥皂。

senses.title: Well-born, of good family
senses.definition: belonging to a family of high social rank
senses.definitionCN: 出身于社会地位高的家庭
senses.example: In old tales only gentle blood could ride in tournaments.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老的故事里，只有高贵血统才能参加骑士比武。
senses.why: This is the word's original sense, social rank, later softened into manners.
senses.whyCN: 这是词的本义——社会等级，后来软化成举止义。

senses.title: Tamed and easy to handle
senses.definition: docile and not wild, as of animals
senses.definitionCN: 温顺不野性，用于动物
senses.example: The gentle mare let the children brush her.
senses.exampleCN: 温顺的母马任由孩子们刷毛。
senses.why: A creature taught by gentle hands becomes gentle, closing the circle of the word.
senses.whyCN: 被温柔之手调教的生灵变得温顺，词义在此完成闭环。

senses.title: To calm or tame someone
senses.definition: to make someone calmer or less angry, especially a horse
senses.definitionCN: 使某人平静或缓和怒气，尤指驯马
senses.example: The trainer gentled the young colt in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 驯马师一周内驯服了小马。
senses.why: The adjective turned verb names the act of producing gentleness.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转动词，命名「制造温柔」的行为。

senses.title: Gradual and moderate in change
senses.definition: changing slowly and not steeply, as slopes or curves
senses.definitionCN: 坡度或曲线变化缓慢而不陡峭
senses.example: The path follows a gentle rise to the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 小路沿着一段平缓的坡升上山脊。
senses.why: Small force produces small change, so gentle describes the mildest gradients.
senses.whyCN: 小力量造成小变化，gentle 因此描述最平缓的梯度。

intro.en: Gentle descends from Latin gentilis, meaning of the same clan, later refined in French.
intro.cn: gentle 源自拉丁语 gentilis（同族的），后经法语精细化。

items.en: Latin gens meant clan, and gentilis meant belonging to the same clan.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gens 意为氏族，gentilis 意为同氏族的。

items.en: Gentilis also translated Greek for foreign nations, gentile.
items.cn: gentilis 还用于翻译希腊语的「异邦人」，即 gentile。

items.en: Old French gentil meant noble, well-born, and refined.
items.cn: 古法语 gentil 意为高贵的、出身好的、有教养的。

items.en: Middle English gentil covered birth, manners, and even the gentle folk as a class.
items.cn: 中古英语 gentil 兼指出身、举止，甚至作为一个阶层的「上等人」。

items.en: Modern English split off gentleman, gentile, and genteel from the same stem.
items.cn: 现代英语从同一词干分出 gentleman、gentile 与 genteel。

note.en: Gentle, genteel, and gentile are triplets from one Latin parent, and soft is its everyday rival.
note.cn: gentle、genteel、gentile 是同一拉丁父母的三个孩子，soft 是它的日常对手。

entries.definition: polite in a showy, old-fashioned way
entries.definitionCN: 斯文做作的；同根的旧式礼貌词

entries.definition: a person not of the Jewish faith
entries.definitionCN: 非犹太人；同根但语义转向宗教

entries.definition: in a mild way
entries.definitionCN: 轻柔地；gentle 的副词

entries.definition: not strong or severe
entries.definitionCN: 温和的；程度偏轻

entries.definition: caring and friendly
entries.definitionCN: 友善的；强调善意

entries.definition: not hard or rough
entries.definitionCN: 柔软的；偏重触感与音量

normalIntro.en: Five grounded hooks for gentle.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词形的 gentle 记忆钩子。

normal.en: Latin gens means clan, so gentle once meant born of a good clan.
normal.cn: 拉丁 gens 意为氏族，gentle 曾指「出自好氏族」。

normal.en: Gentle and gentile differ by one letter and one thousand years of meaning.
normal.cn: gentle 与 gentile 只差一个字母，词义却分道一千年。

normal.en: A gentle slope rises slowly, keeping the mild-force idea.
normal.cn: gentle slope 缓缓上升，保留「力量轻微」之意。

normal.en: Gentle giant pairs huge size with soft manners.
normal.cn: gentle giant 把巨大身躯与柔软举止配对。

normal.en: Be gentle with the puppy, one phrase children hear daily.
normal.cn: be gentle with the puppy 是孩子天天听到的叮嘱。

abstract.en: A hand cupped around a moth, touching without pressing.
abstract.cn: 手掌环住飞蛾，触碰而不按压。

abstract.en: Hear the soft g like a whisper at the start of the word.
abstract.cn: 词首软音 g 像一声耳语。

abstract.en: A candle flame that bends in the faintest draught.
abstract.cn: 烛火在微风中轻轻弯腰。

examples.en: Hold the kitten gently with both hands.
examples.cn: 用双手轻轻抱住小猫。

examples.en: The gentle rain did the garden good.
examples.cn: 温柔的春雨对园子大有好处。

examples.en: He was gentle with the frightened horse.
examples.cn: 他对受惊的马十分温柔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尖头」——温柔的人连说话都是尖头软语的。

root: 拉丁 gens（氏族）→ gentilis（同族的）→ 古法语 gentil（高贵的）→ 英语 gentle；词义路线：高贵出身 → 有教养 → 温柔轻柔；与 genteel、gentile 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Good birth is the starting point; soft force, animals, calming, and slow gradients branch from it.
sensesIntro.cn: 良好出身是起点；轻柔之力、驯化、安抚与缓坡都由此分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trained hand that touches without hurting
core.cn: 核心意象：触碰而不伤害的教养之手

branches.en: kindness of manner
small, mild amounts of force or change
the original rank sense
taming and being tamed
birth refined into behaviour

intro.en: Gentle anchors a triple branch of the gens family in English.
intro.cn: gentle 是 gens 词族在英语中的三叉分支之一。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives keep the clan-and-birth stem visible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词让「氏族与出生」词干清晰可见。

items.exampleCN: gens 曾指罗马家族集团。

items.example: Gentilis is the shared parent of the triplets.
items.exampleCN: gentilis 是三胞胎词的共同父母。

items.example: Her genteel accent fooled no one.
items.exampleCN: 她做作的口音骗不了谁。

items.example: The gentile nations appear in old maps of belief.
items.exampleCN: 旧信仰地图上标注着外邦民族。

items.example: The gentry owned the river meadows.

definition_zh: 诗；诗歌；诗一般的事物
definition_en: a piece of writing arranged in lines, usually with rhythm and often with rhyme, that expresses feeling or thought; the form such works belong to; and something so beautiful or moving that it seems like one
core_image: 一页纸上短行错落，行末的字轻轻碰到一起
scene: 夜里灯下摊着一本薄薄的诗集，行与行之间留出大片空白。 She read the poem twice before she understood why it ended with a question.
sceneCN: 这里 poem 是「诗、诗歌」（第 1 个义项：分行排列、讲究节奏的单篇作品）；句意为她读了两遍，才明白这首诗为什么以一个问句收尾。图中可辨识物件：诗集、台灯、行间的大片留白。

derivatives.zh: 与 poem 同出希腊语 poiein（制作），经拉丁语 poeta 进入英语，义为「诗人」
由 poet 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「诗的；富有诗意的」

senses.title: A piece of writing in lines
senses.definition: a piece of writing arranged in short lines, usually with rhythm and often with rhyme, that expresses feeling or thought
senses.definitionCN: 分行排列、通常讲究节奏并常有押韵、用来表达情感或想法的作品
senses.example: He copied the poem into the back of his notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那首诗抄在笔记本的末页。
senses.why: Greek poiein meant to make, and a poem was first simply a thing made; what made it special was the shaping of words into measured lines rather than any subject matter.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 poiein 意为制作，诗最初只是「做出来的东西」；使它特别的不是题材，而是把词语排成有节度的行。

senses.title: Verse writing as a form
senses.definition: the form of writing that such works belong to, considered as a genre beside prose and drama
senses.definitionCN: 这类作品所属的写作形式，与散文、戏剧并列的一种文体
senses.example: The poem as a form survived the rise of the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 诗歌作为一种文体，在小说兴起之后依然存续。
senses.why: Once a single made thing is recognised, the whole kind it belongs to can be named by the same word, so poem can stand for the form itself, not just one copy of it.
senses.whyCN: 单件「做出来的东西」一旦被认出来，它所属的整类也能用同一个词来指，于是 poem 能指这种文体本身，而不只是其中一件。

senses.title: Something as beautiful as a poem
senses.titleCN: 诗一般的事物；极美之物
senses.definition: something so beautiful, moving or finely made that it seems like a poem
senses.definitionCN: 美、动人或者做得精巧到像诗一样的事物
senses.example: The garden after rain was a poem in green and silver.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后的园子是一首由绿与银写成的诗。
senses.why: Because a poem is the most compressed and ordered use of language, any scene with the same order and economy can be praised by calling it a poem.
senses.whyCN: 诗是语言最凝练、最有秩序的一种用法，因此任何具备同样秩序与节制的景象，都可以被称作一首诗来称赞。

intro.en: Poem goes back to a Greek verb meaning to make; the thing made became a work in verse, and the word travelled through Latin and French into English.
intro.cn: poem 上溯到一个意为「制作」的希腊语动词；被做出来的东西后来指韵文作品，这个词再经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.en: Greek poiein meant to make, to produce or to compose, and it could be used of any craft, not only of writing.
items.cn: 希腊语 poiein 意为制作、产出、创作，可用于任何手艺，并不限于写作。

items.en: The noun poiema named a thing made, a piece of work, and in time it narrowed to a work composed in verse.
items.cn: 名词 poiema 指做出来的东西、一件作品，后来收窄为用韵文写成的作品。

items.en: Latin borrowed poiema as poema, keeping the sense of a poem or a piece of verse, and passed it to the learned writers of Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 poiema 借作 poema，保留了诗、韵文作品的意思，并把它传给欧洲的文人。

items.en: Old French poeme carried the word into ordinary literary use, and English took it over in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 poeme 把这个词带入普通的文学用语，英语在十六世纪把它借了过来。

items.en: Modern English keeps poem for a single work, poetry for the art as a whole, and poet for the maker, all from the same Greek verb.
items.cn: 现代英语用 poem 指单篇作品，用 poetry 指这门艺术整体，用 poet 指创作者，三者同出一个希腊语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek verb for making and the family it produced; the near-meaning group gathers kinds of verse and the parts of verse craft.
note.cn: 形近组沿希腊语表示「制作」的动词及其词族展开；近义组收各种诗体与作诗手法。

entries.definition: A person who writes poems; the Greek maker became the maker of verse.
entries.definitionCN: 写诗的人；希腊语里「制作的人」成了作诗的人。

entries.definition: Poems considered as a whole, or the art of writing them.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的诗歌，或写诗这门艺术。

entries.definition: Relating to poems, or having the beauty and compression of verse.
entries.definitionCN: 与诗有关的，或具有诗的美的凝练。

entries.definition: The study or theory of poetry as a craft.
entries.definitionCN: 把诗当作一门手艺来研究的学问或理论。

entries.definition: Writing arranged in lines with rhythm, or one line of such writing.
entries.definitionCN: 按节奏分行排列的文字，或其中的一行。

entries.definition: A short poem expressing personal feeling, or the words of a song.
entries.definitionCN: 表达个人情感的短诗，或歌词。

entries.definition: A poem of fourteen lines with a fixed pattern of rhyme.
entries.definitionCN: 十四行、押韵格式固定的诗。

entries.definition: A matching of word endings in sound, or a short poem that uses it.
entries.definitionCN: 词尾读音相合，或使用这种相合的小诗。

normalIntro.en: The whole family grows from one Greek verb for making, so poem, poet and poetry all carry the idea of something crafted rather than merely spoken.
normalIntro.cn: 整族词都从一个希腊语表示「制作」的动词长出来，所以 poem、poet、poetry 都带着「被精心做出来」而不是随口说出的意味。

normal.en: Greek poiein means to make, so a poem is literally something made, like a table or a pot.
normal.cn: 希腊语 poiein 意为制作，所以 poem 字面上就是一件做出来的东西，像桌子或陶罐。

normal.en: Poiema is the thing made, and poema is its Latin form; both point to a finished piece of work rather than to inspiration.
normal.cn: poiema 是做出来的东西，poema 是它的拉丁形式；两者都指向一件完成的作品，而不是灵感。

normal.en: Poet, poem and poetry share the stem: the maker, the single work, and the art as a whole.
normal.cn: poet、poem、poetry 共用一个词干：做的人、单件作品，以及整体的艺术。

normal.en: The difference between poem and poetry is the difference between one chair and carpentry.
normal.cn: poem 与 poetry 的区别，就像一把椅子和木工这门手艺的区别。

normal.en: The word has two syllables, and the second is weak; the plural is simply poems.
normal.cn: 这个词有两个音节，第二个音节很轻；复数直接加 s 变成 poems。

abstract.en: A poem is speech that has been made to slow down, so each word can be looked at.
abstract.cn: 诗是被放慢的说话，好让每个词都值得看一眼。

abstract.en: Line breaks are breaths written down, which is why a poem looks different before it is read aloud.
abstract.cn: 分行是写下来的呼吸，所以一首诗在朗读之前，看上去就不一样。

abstract.en: Calling a garden a poem is a way of saying that order and feeling arrived at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 把园子叫作诗，是在说秩序与情感在同一刻到齐了。

examples.en: He copied the poem into the back of his notebook.
examples.cn: 他把那首诗抄在笔记本的末页。

examples.en: The poem as a form survived the rise of the novel.
examples.cn: 诗歌作为一种文体，在小说兴起之后依然存续。

examples.en: The garden after rain was a poem in green and silver.
examples.cn: 雨后的园子是一首由绿与银写成的诗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖木」——把一块木头剖开，削成一行行短句；记住 poem 是诗。

root: 希腊语 poiein（制作）造出 poiema（做出来的东西），拉丁语借作 poema（诗），经古法语 poeme 进入英语；同族有 poet（诗人）、poetry（诗歌总称）、poetic（诗的）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something deliberately made; the senses run from one crafted work in lines, to the whole form of verse writing, and then outward to anything ordered and moving enough to be called a poem.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被有意做出来的东西；义项从一件分行写成的作品，走到韵文写作这种文体，再向外扩展到任何具备同样秩序与动人力量、足以被称作诗的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: short lines stopping well before the margin, with wide white space between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：短行在页边之前就停住，行与行之间留着大片空白。

branches.en: a line ending short of the margin
a page with wide white gaps between the lines
branches.cn: 行间留着大片空白的书页

branches.en: slim volumes of one genre on a shelf
branches.cn: 书架上同一体裁的薄册

branches.en: a critic setting verse beside prose
branches.cn: 评论者把韵文与散文并置

branches.en: a garden shining green after rain

intro.en: The word is built on a Greek verb of making and the noun for the thing made, and the same stem gives English the maker, the art and the adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在希腊语表示「制作」的动词与表示「做成之物」的名词上，同一词干又给出英语里的创作者、这门艺术与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms are recorded for this word: the borrowed noun poema, a poem, and poeta, the maker of one.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词有可考的拉丁形式：借入的名词 poema（诗）与 poeta（作诗的人）。

definition_zh: 政府；政体；治理行为；（英式）内阁、当权者；一届政府
definition_en: the group of people and institutions that direct a state, or the system by which a state is directed
core_image: 一栋办公楼里，部长们在长桌前签署文件，门外是等待答复的市民与记者
scene: 选票清点完毕的第二天，各部门才把拖欠已久的数字挂到网站上。 The government published the figures only after the votes were counted.
sceneCN: 这里 government 指掌握行政权的政府机关（第 1 个义项：作为机构整体）；句意为政府直到计票结束之后才公布那些数字。

pos.zh: 政府；政体（可数，指一届政府或一种政体；不可数，指治理这件事）

derivatives.zh: 政府的（government + -al「……的」，由机关转指其属性）
统治；治理（拉丁 gubernare「掌舵」，由动作本身指操持事务）
治理（govern + -ance「活动」，由机关转指过程）
反政府的（anti-「反对」+ government，由机关转指对立立场）

senses.title: The governing institutions
senses.definition: the body of institutions that direct public affairs and hold executive authority
senses.definitionCN: 主导公共事务并持有行政权威的整套机构
senses.example: The government employs a third of the town's adults.
senses.exampleCN: 政府雇用了镇上三分之一的成年人。
senses.why: -ment first named the result of governing, and the result came to mean the body that does it.
senses.whyCN: -ment 先指治理的结果，结果义再转指做出这个结果的机关。

senses.title: The form of rule
senses.definition: the system by which a state is organized, such as a monarchy or a republic
senses.definitionCN: 组织国家的制度，如君主制或共和制
senses.example: They compared two forms of government across the same century.
senses.exampleCN: 他们比较了同一世纪里的两种政体。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the older meaning of direction as a system rather than a set of persons.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了较早的意思：治理是一套制度，而非一群人。

senses.title: The act of governing
senses.definition: the activity of directing a state, as distinct from the bodies that carry it out
senses.definitionCN: 主导国家的活动，区别于执行它的机构
senses.example: Good government is measured in decades, not in news cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 治理的好坏以十年计，不以新闻周期计。
senses.why: English kept the action reading alongside the institutional one, so the word can name a practice.
senses.whyCN: 英语把行为义与机构义并存下来，因此这个词也能指一种实践。

senses.title: The ministers in office
senses.definition: in parliamentary usage, the prime minister and the ministers currently in office
senses.definitionCN: 在议会制用法中，指在任的首相与各部部长
senses.example: The government lost the motion by four votes.
senses.exampleCN: 内阁以四票之差输掉了动议。
senses.why: in a parliamentary system the executive sits inside the legislature, so the word narrowed to the ministers.
senses.whyCN: 在议会制中行政权坐于立法机关之内，于是这个词收窄为各部部长。

senses.title: One administration
senses.definition: a particular team holding office between one election and the next
senses.definitionCN: 在一次选举与下一次选举之间任职的特定班底
senses.example: Three governments fell within two years.
senses.exampleCN: 两年内倒掉了三届政府。
senses.why: counting administrations requires a countable noun, and this sense supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 要数「届」，就需要一个可数名词，这个义项正好提供。

senses.title: State intervention
senses.titleCN: 政府对经济与社会的干预
senses.definition: the scope of the state's active role in the economy and in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 国家在经济与日常生活中主动介入的范围
senses.example: Arguments about big government are arguments about that scope.
senses.exampleCN: 关于大政府的争论，就是关于这个范围的争论。
senses.why: the word can stand for the state's reach, which is what political argument actually disputes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以代表国家触及的范围，而政治争论争的正是这个范围。

senses.title: Self-command
senses.definition: the old sense of holding one's own conduct under control
senses.definitionCN: 把自身行为置于控制之下的旧义
senses.example: The old manuals praised government of the passions.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手册称赞对激情的自制。
senses.why: the helm image once pointed inward too, and the dictionaries record this sense from the sixteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 舵的意象也曾指向内部，词典自 16 世纪起收录此义。

senses.title: Issued by official authority
senses.titleCN: 作为修饰语：官方的、政府签发的
senses.definition: used before a noun for something issued or owned by the state
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，指由国家签发或持有的
senses.example: Government buildings line the avenue.
senses.exampleCN: 大道两旁都是政府建筑。
senses.why: attributive use lets the noun mark the source of a thing, a very common English pattern.
senses.whyCN: 定语用法让这个名词标示某物的来源，是英语中极常见的模式。

intro.en: Government is govern plus the Latin-derived suffix -ment, modelled on French gouvernement. The suffix first meant the result or means of an action, then the body that performs it. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: government 是 govern 加拉丁系后缀 -ment，仿法语 gouvernement 构成。该后缀先指动作的结果或手段，再指执行动作的机关。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gubernare 'to steer a ship' supplied the verb, and its metaphorical sense of directing people was already Latin.
items.cn: gubernare「操船」提供了动词，其「引导人」的隐喻义在拉丁语中已有。

items.en: Old French gouvernement meant 'administration, direction' in the fourteenth century, with the stress on the activity.
items.cn: 古法语 gouvernement 在 14 世纪指「管理、指引」，重心在活动本身。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century as the act of governing, keeping the abstract sense alive beside the concrete one.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入，指治理这一行为，使抽象义与具体义并存。

items.en: By the sixteenth century government commonly named the persons and bodies that rule, a shift from doing to the doers.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，government 常指统治的人与机关，重心从「做」转到「做的人」。

items.en: In parliamentary usage the word narrowed further to the ministers in office, while American usage kept it for the whole executive branch.
items.cn: 在议会制用法中，这个词进一步收窄为在任部长；美式用法则保留指整个行政部门。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation for the institutional sense is not precisely dated, and the pre-Greek origin of the steering verb behind gubernare is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：机构义的最早英语书证没有确切年代；gubernare 背后那个操船动词在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one shares the govern stem; group two holds words for the state and for rule.
note.cn: 第一组共享 govern 词干；第二组是关于国家与统治的词。

entries.definition: The practice and quality of directing, including accountability; government names the body that holds authority.
entries.definitionCN: 引导的实践与品质，含问责；government 指持有权威的机关。

entries.definition: To direct or rule; the noun adds the institutional result of that activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指引或统治；名词加上这一活动所形成的机构结果。

entries.definition: A single official heading a state or institution; it names one seat, not the whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 领导一州或一机构的单个官员；指一个席位，而非整体。

entries.definition: Of a governor, from Latin gubernator; the form looks foreign but belongs to the same helm family.
entries.definitionCN: 指州长的，来自拉丁 gubernator；词形看着陌生，却属同一个舵的词族。

entries.definition: The political entity as a whole, including territory and people; government is only its directing apparatus.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的政治实体，含领土与人民；government 只是它的主导机关。

entries.definition: In American usage a president's team in office; elsewhere it means management, so it is narrower than government.
entries.definitionCN: 美式用法指总统的执政班底；其他地方指管理，因此比 government 更窄。

entries.definition: A system of rule, often with a hint of harshness or of recent imposition; government is the plainer word.
entries.definitionCN: 一套统治秩序，常暗含严苛或新近强加之意；government 是更中性的说法。

entries.definition: The legal or accepted power to act; government is the body that normally holds such power.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的法律或公认权力；government 通常就是持有此种权力的机关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: govern + -ment: first the result of steering, then the body that steers.
normal.cn: govern + -ment：先是操舵的结果，再是操舵的机关。

normal.en: The family runs govern, government, governor, governance, governmental.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 govern、government、governor、governance、governmental。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: form a government, coalition government, local government.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：组阁、联合政府、地方政府。

normal.en: Countable and uncountable split matters: three governments fell, but government is necessary.
normal.cn: 可数与否的分野很关键：倒了三届政府，但治理本身是必要的。

normal.en: British news says the government lost the vote; American news says the administration did.
normal.cn: 英媒说内阁输掉表决，美媒说执政班底输掉表决。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where the same five people sign for a whole country.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，同样五个人替整个国家签字。

abstract.en: Picture a building that changes tenants but keeps the same letterhead.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋楼换了租客，信笺抬头却始终不变。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a tiller that must answer to a queue outside the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着舵，还得向门外的队列交代。

examples.en: The government raised the levy without warning the growers.
examples.cn: 政府加征费用，却没有事先通知种植者。

examples.en: Coalition governments tend to postpone unpopular decisions.
examples.cn: 联合政府往往把不得人心的决定往后拖。

examples.en: Local government carries most of the cost of the repairs.
examples.cn: 地方政府承担了修缮的大部分费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: govern（掌舵）+ ment（机构）＝ 替国家扶舵的那套班子；记「换班子不换舵」。

root: govern + -ment：govern 经古法语 governer 上溯拉丁 gubernare「操船、治理」，再上溯希腊 kybernan「掌舵」，后者更早来源不确定；-ment 源自拉丁 -mentum「结果、手段」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one helm through time: the act of steering, the system of steering, the body that steers, the ministers inside that body, one team in office, the state's reach, steering oneself, and the attributive mark of official origin.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一具舵柄穿过时间：操舵的行为、操舵的制度、操舵的机关、机关里的部长、一届执政班底、国家触及的范围、对自己操舵，以及标示官方来源的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a national tiller, inside a building that outsiders stand outside of.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手扶着国家的舵，人在一栋楼里，外人站在楼外。

branches.en: DOING AND DOERS: the practice and the body are the same word seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 做与做的人：实践与机关是同一个词的两面。

branches.en: THE RULEBOOK: the form of rule outlives every team that works it.
branches.cn: 规则书：政体比任何操作它的班底都活得久。

branches.en: INSIDE THE BUILDING: the ministers, then the particular team counting as one unit.
branches.cn: 楼内：先是部长们，再是被算作一个单位的特定班底。

branches.en: REACH: how far the state's hand extends into the economy.
branches.cn: 触及范围：国家这只手伸进经济多深。

branches.en: INWARD AND ADJECTIVAL: steering oneself, and marking a thing as officially issued.
branches.cn: 向内与定语：对自己操舵，以及标示某物由官方签发。

intro.en: Government is one Latin verb plus one Latin suffix, and both parts build a large English family.
intro.cn: government 是一个拉丁动词加一个拉丁后缀，两部分都构成不小的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Gubernare yields govern, governor and gubernatorial; -mentum yields government, argument and monument.
latinIntro.cn: gubernare 衍生 govern、governor、gubernatorial；-mentum 衍生 government、argument、monument。

items.example: The verb pictures a hand on the helm.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词画出扶舵的手。

items.meaning: result or means of an action

definition_zh: 影响；影响力；影响者
definition_en: the power to change how someone acts or thinks without using force
core_image: 看不见的风把树叶吹向一侧
scene: 老师随口的一句评语，让少年重新拿起了画笔。 Parents have a strong influence on children.
sceneCN: 这里 influence 是「影响」（第 1 个义项：改变他人的力量）；句意：父母对孩子有很大影响。

derivatives.zh: influence 加形容词后缀，义为「有影响力的」
influence 加施动者后缀，义为「网红；有影响的人」
同源词，义为「流感」（旧义「星象影响」）

senses.title: Power to change others
senses.definition: the power to change how someone acts or thinks without force
senses.definitionCN: 不用强力就能改变他人行动或想法的力量
senses.example: Parents have a strong influence on children.
senses.exampleCN: 父母对孩子有很大影响。
senses.why: An unseen wind bends the leaves.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的风吹弯了树叶。

senses.title: A person or thing that shapes
senses.titleCN: 影响者；产生影响的事物
senses.definition: someone or something that shapes another
senses.definitionCN: 塑造他人的人或事物
senses.example: That book was a great influence in her life.
senses.exampleCN: 那本书对她一生影响极大。
senses.why: The wind itself gets a name.
senses.whyCN: 这阵风本身也有了名字。

senses.title: To sway or shape
senses.definition: to change someone's behavior or a result quietly
senses.definitionCN: 悄悄改变某人的行为或某个结果
senses.example: Advertising influences what we buy.
senses.exampleCN: 广告左右着我们的购买。
senses.why: The wind is released at the leaves.
senses.whyCN: 风被释放到树叶上。

senses.title: Under the influence: drunk
senses.definition: affected by alcohol, a fixed legal phrase
senses.definitionCN: 受酒精作用，法律固定短语
senses.example: He was arrested for driving under the influence.
senses.exampleCN: 他因酒后驾车被捕。
senses.why: The wind inside the bottle steers the car.
senses.whyCN: 瓶中的风替他掌了方向盘。

intro.en: Influence comes from medieval Latin influentia, a flowing in. Astrologers first used it for an invisible fluid said to flow from the stars into people, shaping their fates.
intro.cn: influence 来自中世纪拉丁语 influentia「流入」。占星家先用它指从星辰流入人体、左右命运的不可见流体。

items.en: Latin fluere meant to flow; it gave fluid, fluent and fluent rivers of words.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fluere 意为流动；同根词有 fluid、fluent 等。

items.en: in- plus fluere formed influere: to flow in.
items.cn: in- 加 fluere 构成 influere：流入。

items.en: influentia named the star-fluid that shaped human fate.
items.cn: influentia 指塑造人命运的星辰流体。

items.en: Old French influence passed the astrological sense to English.
items.cn: 古法语 influence 把占星义传给英语。

items.en: Modern English dropped the stars and kept the invisible shaping power.
items.cn: 现代英语去掉了星辰，只留下那股无形的塑造之力。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the flow-root family. The meaning group compares words of quiet power.
note.cn: 形近组收录「流动」词根词族；词义组比较表示无形力量的词。

entries.definition: having great influence.
entries.definitionCN: 有影响力的。

entries.definition: flu; from the same flowing-in idea.
entries.definitionCN: 流感，同出「流入」之意。

entries.definition: flowing smoothly, of speech.
entries.definitionCN: 流利的，同样出自流动词根。

entries.definition: a strong, often sudden effect.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈且常突然的作用。

entries.definition: the result of a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 原因造成的结果。

entries.definition: control over opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 对舆论的支配。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the star-fluid origin, the flow root and the legal phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用星辰流体词源、流动词根与法律短语。

normal.en: in- plus fluere (flow): an invisible current flows in.
normal.cn: in- 加 fluere（流动）：一股看不见的水流流入。

normal.en: Astrologers thought star-fluid shaped your fate.
normal.cn: 占星家认为星辰流体塑造命运。

normal.en: have an influence on is the exam pattern.
normal.cn: have an influence on 是考试句式。

normal.en: driving under the influence means drunk driving.
normal.cn: driving under the influence 即酒驾。

normal.en: influent people and influencer share the root.
normal.cn: influential 与 influencer 共享词根。

abstract.en: One image: wind that no eye sees bending every leaf.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：无人看见的风吹弯了每片叶子。

abstract.en: Influence is force without a push.
abstract.cn: influence 是不用推搡的力量。

abstract.en: A river entering a lake quietly changes its color.
abstract.cn: 一条河悄悄入湖，改变了湖水的颜色。

examples.en: Teachers have a lasting influence on students.
examples.cn: 老师对学生有持久的影响。

examples.en: The moon influences the tides.
examples.cn: 月亮影响潮汐。

examples.en: He was charged with driving under the influence.
examples.cn: 他被控酒后驾驶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因fluence（富润斯）」：富人有润物无声的影响力， influence。

root: 拉丁语 in-「流入」+ fluere「流动」→ 中世纪拉丁语 influentia「星辰流入人体的流体」→ 古法语 influence → 现代英语 influence「无形的影响」；同根词 fluid、fluent、fluctuate。

sensesIntro.en: Influence is the star-fluid turned everyday: a power that flows in, the person carrying it, the quiet act of shaping, and the bottle that steers a car.
sensesIntro.cn: influence 是走进日常的星辰流体：流入的力量、携风之人、悄然塑造的动作，以及替人掌舵的酒瓶。

core.en: An invisible current that flows in and bends what it touches.
core.cn: 一股看不见的水流，流入并使所触之物弯曲。

branches.en: POWER: parents shape children.
AGENT: the book was a great influence.
branches.cn: 影响者：那本书影响极大。

branches.en: ACTION: advertising influences what we buy.
INTOXICATION: driving under the influence.
SHAPING: fate bent without force.
branches.cn: 塑造：命运不经强力而被改变。

intro.en: Influence builds influential, influencer and keeps influenza in the family.
intro.cn: influence 构成 influential、influencer， influenza 亦属同族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the flowing verb fluere behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示词族背后的流动动词 fluere。

items.exampleCN: 一篇有影响的论文改变了政策。

latinEntries.meaning: a flowing in; star-fluid shaping fate
latinEntries.meaningCN: 流入；左右命运的星辰流体

definition_zh: 供应；供应量
definition_en: to provide something needed, or the amount provided
core_image: 一辆货车把新鲜蔬菜卸到商店门口
scene: 这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。 The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.
sceneCN: 这里 supply 是「供应」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。

derivatives.zh: 供应商
补给品
补充物

senses.title: To provide
senses.definition: to give or sell something that is needed
senses.definitionCN: 给出或出售所需要的东西
senses.example: The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。
senses.why: This is the main verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的动词义项。

senses.title: The amount available
senses.definition: the amount of something available
senses.definitionCN: 可获得的东西的数量
senses.example: The water supply is limited.
senses.exampleCN: 供水是有限的。
senses.why: Here the word is a noun of amount.
senses.whyCN: 这里指数量的名词。

senses.title: Goods for a need
senses.definition: food and equipment needed for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某一目的需要的食物与装备
senses.example: They carried medical supplies.
senses.exampleCN: 他们携带医疗物资。
senses.why: This plural sense names concrete goods.
senses.whyCN: 这个复数义项指具体物资。

intro.en: Supply comes from Latin supplere, to fill up.
intro.cn: supply 来自拉丁语 supplere，意为填满、补足。

items.en: Sub meant under.
items.cn: sub 意为在下。

items.en: Plere meant to fill.
items.cn: plere 意为填满。

items.en: Suppleer meant to fill a need.
items.cn: suppleer 意为满足需要。

items.en: Supply meant to provide.
items.cn: supply 意为提供。

items.en: It also meant the amount provided.
items.cn: 它也指所提供的数量。

note.en: Supply is compared with look-alike words and with verbs of providing.

entries.definition: to ask formally or to put on

entries.definition: to answer

entries.definition: to add to something

entries.definition: to give what is needed

entries.definition: to supply or equip

entries.definition: to bring to a place

normalIntro.en: To supply is to fill the empty space in someone's need.
normalIntro.cn: supply 就是填满别人需求里的空位。

normal.en: The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.

normal.en: They carried medical supplies.

normal.en: Demand is rising faster than supply.

normal.en: Fresh water is in short supply here.

abstract.en: Supply is a promise made in goods.
abstract.cn: 供应，是用货物许下的承诺。

abstract.en: A chain of supply is a chain of trust.

definition_zh: 工厂；制造厂
definition_en: a building or organization where goods are manufactured in large quantities
core_image: 流水线上一排机械臂此起彼伏，传送带把零件送进、把成品送出
scene: 参观日，学生戴上安全帽，隔着玻璃看机器人手臂焊接车壳。 Through the glass the students watched the robots weld car bodies in the factory.
sceneCN: 这里指「制造商品的场所」，对应第 1 个义项：批量生产货物的建筑；句意为学生隔玻璃观看工厂里机器人焊接车身。画面要点：安全帽、玻璃隔断、机械臂火花。

derivatives.zh: 制造（拉丁 manu「手」加词根 fac「做」，本义手工制作，今指批量生产）
制造业（动词的名词化）
工厂复数（基础词加复数变化）
因素（同根词，指起作用的成分）
轻易的（同根形容词，指容易做到的）

senses.title: A building where goods are made
senses.definition: a large building or group of buildings where goods are manufactured
senses.definitionCN: 批量制造商品的大型建筑或建筑群
senses.example: The factory turns out toys every day.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂每天生产玩具。
senses.why: The place sense grew directly from the Latin 'place of doing'; making goods is just doing, organized.
senses.whyCN: 场所义直接从拉丁语「做事之地」长出；造货就是把「做」组织化。

senses.title: The workers and system of production
senses.definition: the organization and workforce of manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 制造业的组织与劳动力
senses.example: The whole factory stopped for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 全厂停工检修。
senses.why: Once a building means organized making, the word covers the people inside it too.
senses.whyCN: 建筑既指有组织的制作，这个词也顺势涵盖其中的人。

senses.title: A place producing one thing in quantity
senses.definition: any site that produces large amounts of a single product
senses.definitionCN: 大量产出单一产品的地方
senses.example: A data factory of numbers
senses.exampleCN: 一座数字的数据工厂
senses.why: Large-scale single output repeats the factory pattern outside industry.
senses.whyCN: 大规模单一产出把工厂模式复制到了工业之外。

intro.en: Factory comes from Latin factorium, a place where things are done or made.
intro.cn: factory 来自拉丁语 factorium，即做东西或办事的场所。

items.en: Latin factorium meant an oil press or a place of business, from factor, a doer.
items.cn: 拉丁语 factorium 指油坊或事务所，来自 factor（做事者）。

items.en: Medieval Latin factorium named trading posts overseas as well as workshops.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 factorium 也用来称呼海外商站。

items.en: Portuguese feitoria kept the overseas trading-post sense in the age of sail.
items.cn: 葡萄牙语 feitoria 在大航海时代保留了海外商站之义。

items.en: French factorerie passed the trading-post sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 factorerie 把商站之义传入英语。

items.en: Modern English settled factory for a building where goods are manufactured by machinery.
items.cn: 现代英语把 factory 固定为用机器批量制造商品的建筑。

note.en: Look-alikes share the Latin root fac-; near-meaning words name places of making.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 fac-；近义组命名「制造场所」。

entries.definition: a thing that acts to produce a result
entries.definitionCN: 起作用的因素；同出拉丁 facere

entries.definition: a thing known to be true
entries.definitionCN: 事实；同根不同缀

entries.definition: an ability or a department
entries.definitionCN: 能力；学院；拼写相近但词源为拉丁 facilitas

entries.definition: a factory, especially for grain or steel
entries.definitionCN: 工厂（多指磨坊、钢铁厂）

entries.definition: a factory for power or heavy industry
entries.definitionCN: 工厂（多指电厂、重工业）

entries.definition: a room or building where manual work is done
entries.definitionCN: 作坊；车间

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the Latin word for a place of making.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「制作场所」的五个抓手。

normal.en: fact (do) plus -ory (place) adds up to a place where things are made.
normal.cn: fact（做）+ -ory（场所）＝做东西的地方。

normal.en: The plural changes y to i: factories, like cities and stories.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变 i：factories，同 cities、stories。

normal.en: car factory and steel factory are everyday pairings in news and traffic.
normal.cn: car factory、steel factory 都是超高频搭配。

normal.en: factory farming means high-density livestock production, common in the papers.
normal.cn: factory farming 指高密度养殖，新闻里常见。

normal.en: factor, fact, and perfect all carry the same Latin verb for doing.
normal.cn: factor、fact、perfect 都含「做」。

abstract.en: A factory is a big standardized box: workers go in, products come out.
abstract.cn: 工厂是把劳动标准化的大盒子：人进去，产品出来。

abstract.en: The assembly line turns time itself into parts, consumed one slot at a time.
abstract.cn: 流水线让时间也变成零件，一格一格被消费。

abstract.en: On every city's edge squat rows of silent giant iron boxes.
abstract.cn: 每个城市的郊区都蹲着一排沉默的巨型铁盒。

examples.en: The chocolate factory smells of cocoa all day.
examples.cn: 巧克力工厂整天飘着可可味。

examples.en: New machines doubled the factory output this year.
examples.cn: 新机器使工厂产量今年翻倍。

examples.en: Her grandfather worked in the factory for thirty years.
examples.cn: 她祖父在这家工厂干了三十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法克特瑞」——法（做）+ 克特（东西）+ 瑞（地方）：做法克东西的地方，就是工厂。

root: 拉丁语 factorium（做事之场所），源自 factor（做事者），后者来自动词 facere（做）。经中世纪拉丁语、葡萄牙语 feitoria 与法语传入英语，词义从商站转移到制造场所。

sensesIntro.en: From a place of doing to the whole system of organized production.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「做事之地」扩展到有组织的生产体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a big organized place where raw things go in and finished goods come out.
core.cn: 核心意象：原料进去、成品出来的大型有组织场所。

branches.en: THE PLACE: the building of manufacture.
THE SYSTEM: people and machines together.
THE SCALE: one product, huge quantity.
branches.cn: 规模：单一产品的大批量。

branches.en: THE ECONOMY: factories as engines of trade.
branches.cn: 经济：工厂作为贸易引擎。

branches.en: THE IMAGE: factory as a metaphor for mindless repetition.
branches.cn: 意象：工厂作为机械重复的隐喻。

intro.en: Factory is fac- (do) plus -ory (place); the suffix family names places and things of doing.
intro.cn: factory 是 fac-（做）加 -ory（场所）；该后缀族命名做事之地与之物。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere gives the root; -ory gives the place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere 给出词根；-ory 给出场所。

items.meaning: to make by hand or machine

definition_zh: 从；来自；由于；与……（不同、区别开）
definition_en: used to show the starting point, source, origin, cause, or separation in space, time, or manner
core_image: 一条起点清晰、向外延伸的路径：人、物或时间从某处出发
scene: 清晨的火车站台上，广播报着班次。 The morning train to Hangzhou departs from platform six, so we still have time for coffee.
sceneCN: 这里 from 表示「从……出发」（第 1 个义项：起点）；句意为开往杭州的早班车从六号站台发车，我们还来得及喝杯咖啡。

derivatives.zh: 与 from 同源的日耳曼词，义为「向前；向外」，语义偏移为方向副词
方向后缀 -ward 构成的副词，义为「朝家的方向」，与 from 的起点语义互补

senses.title: A starting point in space
senses.definition: used to show the place where movement or distance begins
senses.definitionCN: 表示移动或距离开始的地方
senses.example: She walks to school from her grandmother's house.
senses.exampleCN: 她从奶奶家步行去学校。
senses.why: The core picture is a path with a clear origin; the preposition names that origin point.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是一条有明确起点的路径；介词的功能就是标出那个起点。

senses.title: A starting point in time
senses.definition: used to show when something begins
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事开始的时间点
senses.example: The shop is open from nine in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店从早上九点开始营业。
senses.why: Time is imagined as a line, so the same origin-point idea moves from space onto the time line.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一条线，于是「起点」的空间概念迁移到了时间线上。

senses.title: Source or origin
senses.definition: used to show where something comes, is sent, or is obtained
senses.definitionCN: 表示某物来自哪里、由谁寄出或从何处取得
senses.example: This letter is from my pen friend in Canada.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信来自我加拿大的笔友。
senses.why: Things travel like people do; the origin of a thing is treated as its starting point.
senses.whyCN: 物的流动像人的移动一样，物的来源被当作它的出发点来表述。

senses.title: Cause or reason
senses.definition: used to show the cause of a feeling, state, or result
senses.definitionCN: 表示情感、状态或结果的原因
senses.example: He trembled from cold and fear.
senses.exampleCN: 他因寒冷和恐惧而发抖。
senses.why: A cause is imagined as the source from which a state flows out, reusing the origin image.
senses.whyCN: 原因被想象成状态流出的源头，复用「来源」的画面。

senses.title: Raw material
senses.definition: used to show the material something is made of
senses.definitionCN: 表示制成某物所用的材料
senses.example: Paper is made from bamboo and rags in some villages.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些村庄，纸是用竹子和破布做的。
senses.why: The material is the origin of the finished thing, so from marks what the object started as.
senses.whyCN: 原料是成品的来源，因此 from 标记物品最初由什么开始。

senses.title: Separation or difference
senses.definition: used to show that two things are kept apart or are different
senses.definitionCN: 表示两事物被隔开或彼此不同
senses.example: Can you tell real pearls from false ones?
senses.exampleCN: 你能分辨真珍珠与假珍珠吗？
senses.why: To tell one thing from another is to pull them apart at a shared point, reusing the departure image.
senses.whyCN: 区分两者就是在共同点上把它们拉开，复用「离开起点」的画面。

intro.en: From is one of the oldest function words in English, a native preposition whose history is fully Germanic.
intro.cn: from 是英语最古老的功能词之一，是纯日耳曼语系的本土介词。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic adverb and preposition *fr- meant away from, forward.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语副词兼介词 *fr- 表示「离开、向前」。

items.en: Old English fram meant from, forward, and also brave as an adjective.
items.cn: 古英语 fram 既表示「从、向前」，作形容词时还表示「勇敢的」。

items.en: Closely related Old Norse frá reinforced the same preposition in northern speech.
items.cn: 同源的古诺斯语 frá 在北方口语中强化了这一介词。

items.en: Middle English from settled into the standard preposition of origin and separation.
items.cn: 中古英语 from 稳定为表示来源与分离的标准介词。

items.en: Modern English keeps all core uses: point of origin, source, cause, material, and difference.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了全部核心用法：起点、来源、原因、原料与区别。

note.en: From pairs with to, and its Germanic cousins share the same root.
note.cn: from 与 to 成对出现，它的日耳曼近亲词共享同一词根。

entries.definitionCN: 形状；表格；与 from 只是字母顺序不同，词源完全不同

entries.definitionCN: 向前；与 from 同出日耳曼词根，语义偏向方向

entries.definitionCN: 前面；拼写相近但来自拉丁语词根
