normalIntro.en: Five grounded hooks for the preposition from.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实用法的介词 from 记忆钩子。

normal.en: From shares the Germanic fr- head that also moves forward in forth and fro.
normal.cn: from 与 forth、fro 共享日耳曼词头 fr-，都带着「离开、向前」的意味。

normal.en: The collocation from now on is the most frequent, so anchor all others to it.
normal.cn: 搭配 from now on 最常用，先把其他用法都挂在它上面。

normal.en: Tell A from B means pulling A away from B until they are separate.
normal.cn: tell A from B 就是把 A 从 B 身边拉开，直到两者分开。

normal.en: Made from signals a changed material, while made of keeps the material visible.
normal.cn: made from 表示原料已变形，made of 表示材质仍可辨认。

normal.en: From and to form a fixed pair: origin against endpoint.
normal.cn: from 与 to 是固定搭档：起点对终点。

abstract.en: See the exact moment an arrow leaves the bowstring: that point is from.
abstract.cn: 想象箭离弦的一瞬：那个点就是 from。

abstract.en: Treat time as a river; from is where you step in.
abstract.cn: 把时间想成河流，from 是你下水的地点。

abstract.en: Separating two tangled ropes at a knot mirrors telling one thing from another.
abstract.cn: 在绳结处分开两根缠绳，正如区分两件事物。

examples.cn: 这班巴士从车站开往机场。

examples.en: She was tired from working all night.
examples.cn: 她因整夜工作而疲惫。

examples.en: Wine is made from grapes.
examples.cn: 葡萄酒由葡萄酿成。

sensesIntro.en: All senses share one image: a clear starting point from which things, people, time, or causes flow outward.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项共用一个画面：一个清晰的起点，人、物、时间或原因由此向外延展。

intro.cn: from 本身不接词缀，但它的词根族构成了多个日常词。

latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同源词：from 是纯日耳曼词。

items.exampleCN: 古英语 fram 曾用于称赞勇士。

definition_zh: 文件；公文；证件；文献；记录
definition_en: a piece of paper or digital file that gives information or proves something
core_image: 盖着红章的证明文件摆在桌上
scene: 入境大厅前排着长队，他把护照从文件袋里抽出来。 The officer checked every document at the border.
sceneCN: 这里 document 是「证件、文件」（第 1 个义项：证明或提供信息的材料）；句意：边检人员查验每一份证件。

derivatives.zh: document 加后缀构成，义为「纪录片」
document 加名词后缀构成，义为「文档；证明材料」
document 的过去分词作形容词，义为「有据可查的」

senses.title: A paper or file that proves or informs
senses.definition: a written or printed paper, or a digital file, giving proof or information
senses.definitionCN: 提供证明或信息的书面、打印或电子材料
senses.example: Please bring an identity document to the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试请携带身份证件。
senses.why: Latin docere means to teach: a document is a thing that teaches the reader what is true.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 docere 意为「教导」：document 就是向读者「讲明」真相之物。

senses.title: A historical written record
senses.definition: an old written record kept for study
senses.definitionCN: 供研究保存的古老书面记录
senses.example: Historians studied the documents of the Ming court.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家研究明代的宫廷文献。
senses.why: Records preserved in writing keep teaching later generations, so the teaching root survives.
senses.whyCN: 以文字保存的记录持续教导后人，「教导」词根得以延续。

senses.title: To prove or record with evidence
senses.definition: to support a claim with written evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用书面证据支持某个说法
senses.example: The reporter documented every step of the story.
senses.exampleCN: 记者为报道的每一步留档佐证。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: what the paper teaches becomes what the writer records.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：纸上讲明的内容，变成写作者记录的内容。

intro.en: Document began as a Latin word for a lesson: something that teaches.
intro.cn: document 起初是拉丁语里的「课程」：能教导人的东西。

items.en: Latin documentum meant a lesson or warning, from docere, to teach.
items.cn: 拉丁语 documentum 意为课程或警示，来自 docere（教导）。

items.en: The root doc- also gave doctor, doctrine and docile.
items.cn: 词根 doc- 还派生出 doctor、doctrine 与 docile。

items.en: Old French document meant instruction and later a written paper.
items.cn: 古法语 document 先指教导，后指书面文件。

items.en: English borrowed it in the fifteenth century for teaching and proof.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语借入该词，指教导与凭证。

items.en: The word now covers passports, archives and computer files.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖证件、档案与计算机文件。

note.en: These words sit near document in form or meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 document 相邻。

normal.en: Documentation helps new users learn a program.

abstract.en: Hear paper stamps thudding one by one.
abstract.cn: 听盖章声一下一下地闷响。

examples.en: Keep the receipt as a document of your purchase.
examples.cn: 把收据留作购物凭证。

examples.en: All travel documents must be valid for six months.
examples.cn: 所有旅行证件有效期须满六个月。

examples.en: The museum keeps documents from the old dynasty.
examples.cn: 博物馆保存着旧王朝的文献。

definition_zh: 碎片；薯条；芯片；削下碎片；碰缺
definition_en: a small broken piece; a thin fried potato; a tiny electronic circuit; to break a small piece off
core_image: 从大块上崩下来的一小片
scene: 厨房里，妈妈正把土豆切成细条准备炸。 My mother dropped a chip of potato into the hot oil.
sceneCN: 这里 chip 是「薯条」（第 2 个义项：油炸土豆条）；句意是妈妈把一根土豆条放进热油里。

senses.title: A small broken piece
senses.definition: a small piece broken off something hard
senses.definitionCN: 从坚硬物上崩下来的小块
senses.example: A chip of paint fell on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一块油漆碎片掉在地板上。
senses.why: A knock breaks a little piece away from the whole.
senses.whyCN: 一磕碰，就从整体上崩下小片。

senses.title: A thin piece of fried potato
senses.definition: a long thin piece of potato cooked in oil
senses.definitionCN: 油炸的细长土豆条
senses.example: We shared a bag of chips after school.
senses.exampleCN: 放学后我们分吃了一包薯条。
senses.why: The potato is cut into small slips, like chips of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 土豆被切成小条，就像整块上的碎条。

senses.title: A tiny electronic circuit
senses.definition: a very small flat piece inside computers that holds circuits
senses.definitionCN: 计算机内部承载电路的微型薄片
senses.example: This phone uses a faster chip.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手机用了更快的芯片。
senses.why: The little silicon slip is a chip of the whole machine's brain.
senses.whyCN: 这片小小的硅片是机器大脑的一小块。

senses.title: To break a small piece off
senses.definition: to lose or remove a small piece from an edge or surface
senses.definitionCN: 使边缘或表面脱落一小块
senses.example: Don't chip the paint on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 别把课桌上的漆碰掉了。
senses.why: One careless hit takes a bite out of the edge.
senses.whyCN: 一次不小心磕碰就啃掉一块边。

intro.en: Chip has always meant a small piece cut or broken off.
intro.cn: chip 一直表示切下或崩下的小片。

items.en: Old English cipp meant a thin piece of wood, a beam or chip.
items.cn: 古英语 cipp 指薄木片、木条。

items.en: The word kept its wooden sense through the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 整个中世纪该词保留木片之义。

items.en: Wooden chips led to fried potato chips, named for their shape.
items.cn: 木片引申出炸薯条，因其形状得名。

items.en: British English keeps chips for fries; American chips are crisps.
items.cn: 英式 chips 指薯条；美式 chips 指薯片。

items.en: In the twentieth century the tiny silicon circuit borrowed the same small-piece idea.
items.cn: 二十世纪，微型硅电路借用了同一「小片」概念。

note.en: Small pieces and near spellings.

definition_zh: 机场；航空站；空港；机场的
definition_en: a place where planes take off and land, with buildings for travellers
core_image: 跑道上飞机正滑向航站楼
scene: 跑道旁，一架飞机正滑向航站楼。 Our plane landed at the airport on time.
sceneCN: 这里 airport 是「机场」（第 1 个义项：飞机起降的场所）；句意为我们的飞机准时降落在机场。

derivatives.zh: 机场航站楼

senses.title: The place for flights
senses.definition: the whole place where aircraft arrive and leave
senses.definitionCN: 飞机抵达与离开的整个场所
senses.example: Our plane landed at the airport on time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的飞机准时降落在机场。
senses.why: Air plus port moves a harbour into the sky: the place where aircraft come and go.
senses.whyCN: air 加 port，把港口搬到天上，就是飞机起降的场所。

senses.title: The terminal buildings
senses.definition: the buildings where travellers check in and wait
senses.definitionCN: 旅客办手续与等候的建筑物
senses.example: The airport was full of holiday crowds.
senses.exampleCN: 航站楼里挤满了度假的人群。
senses.why: Travellers meet the place through its halls, so the buildings themselves are called the airport.
senses.whyCN: 旅客接触这个场所主要通过大厅，所以建筑群本身也被叫作 airport。

senses.title: A small airfield
senses.definition: a modest field with simple buildings for light planes
senses.definitionCN: 供轻型飞机使用、建筑简单的场地
senses.example: A small airport serves the island.
senses.exampleCN: 一座小型航空站为这个岛服务。
senses.why: The same name is used for a field with only simple buildings.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名称也用在只有简单建筑的场地。

intro.en: The recorded history of airport is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 airport 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Porta meant a gate or a doorway, and it gave the port in this word.
items.cn: porta 意为门或入口，它给出了这个词里的 port。

items.en: English port first named a harbour where ships came and went.
items.cn: 英语 port 最初指船只往来的港口。

items.en: Air named the open sky above the ground.
items.cn: air 指地面之上的开阔天空。

items.en: When planes began to fly, English joined the two words for a field with buildings.
items.cn: 飞机开始飞行后，英语把这两个词结合起来，指带建筑的场地。

definition_zh: 绅士；先生；有教养的男人；（称呼）各位先生
definition_en: a courteous, well-mannered man, or a polite way to address or mention men
core_image: 为身后的人扶住玻璃门、微微颔首的男子
scene: 咖啡馆门开了又合，风铃轻响。 A gentleman held the door for the mother with two children.
sceneCN: 这里 gentleman 是「绅士」（第 1 个义项：彬彬有礼的男人）；句意为一位绅士为带着两个孩子的母亲扶住了门。

senses.title: A courteous, well-mannered man
senses.definition: a man who is polite and behaves well towards others
senses.definitionCN: 待人礼貌、举止得体的男人
senses.example: Only a gentleman returns the extra change.
senses.exampleCN: 只有绅士才会把多找的零钱退回去。
senses.why: Good birth once promised good manners, so the rank word became the behaviour word.
senses.whyCN: 好的出身曾预示好的举止，等级词由此变成行为词。

senses.title: A man of good social standing
senses.definition: a man of good family or social position
senses.definitionCN: 家世或社会地位良好的男人
senses.example: The estate passed to a wealthy gentleman.
senses.exampleCN: 庄园传给了一位富裕的乡绅。
senses.why: This is the older half of the word, rank before manners.
senses.whyCN: 这是词的较旧一半——先有等级，后有举止。

senses.title: A polite way to address a man
senses.definition: a polite word for any man, often with this or that
senses.definitionCN: 对任何男性的礼貌称呼，常与 this、that 连用
senses.example: This gentleman was here first.
senses.exampleCN: 这位先生先到的。
senses.why: Honorifics borrow the rank word to honour strangers politely.
senses.whyCN: 敬称借用等级词来礼貌地抬高陌生人。

senses.title: Men as a group in speeches
senses.definition: men addressed collectively in formal speech
senses.definitionCN: 正式讲话中对男性听众的集体称呼
senses.example: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome aboard.
senses.exampleCN: 女士们、先生们，欢迎登机。
senses.why: The plural ranks the whole room politely, a speech-hall formula.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式礼貌地统称全场，是演讲厅的固定程式。

senses.title: A man who does not need to work
senses.definition: a man of independent means, not a manual worker
senses.definitionCN: 有独立资产、不事体力劳作的男人
senses.example: He lived as a gentleman on rents from the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠庄园租金过着绅士生活。
senses.why: Rank without labour defined the old gentry, so leisure marked the gentleman.
senses.whyCN: 旧乡绅以「有产而无劳」定义，悠闲成了绅士的标志。

intro.en: Gentleman is a compound of gentle and man, first written for men of noble birth.
intro.cn: gentleman 是 gentle 与 man 的复合词，最初记录用于指贵族出身的男子。

items.en: Old French gentil supplied the noble half of the compound.
items.cn: 古法语 gentil 提供了复合词中「高贵」的一半。

items.en: Old English mann supplied the person half.
items.cn: 古英语 mann 提供了「人」的一半。

items.en: Middle English gentil man meant a man of good family.
items.cn: 中古英语 gentil man 指家世良好的男子。

items.en: The sense slid from birth to manners across the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪前后词义从出身滑向举止。

items.en: Modern English fixed gentleman as courteous man and polite address.
items.cn: 现代英语把 gentleman 定型为「有礼的男士」与敬称。

note.en: Gentleman, sir, and lord divide the politeness field among them.
note.cn: gentleman、sir、lord 分占了礼貌用语的不同领地。

definition_zh: 期待；预计；要求；料想；怀有身孕
definition_en: to believe that something will happen, to await it, or to require it as a duty
core_image: 一个人站在门口向外望，手里已经握住门把
scene: 站台上，家长不断看表，孩子乘坐的列车还有十分钟到站。 She did not expect the train to be so crowded.
sceneCN: 这里 expect 指「料想某事会发生」（第 1 个义项：认为某事将会发生）；句意为他没想到列车会这么拥挤。场景要素：站台、看表的手、到站显示屏。

derivatives.zh: 由 expect 加名词后缀构成，指预期或期望的事物
由 expect 加过去分词词尾构成，指按计划应当发生的
由否定前缀加 expected 构成，指出乎意料的
由 expect 加形容词后缀构成，指期待着的或即将为人父母的

senses.title: Believe something will happen
senses.definition: to think that an event is likely to happen, on the basis of evidence or habit
senses.definitionCN: 基于证据或习惯，认为某事件很可能会发生
senses.example: Economists expect a slight fall in exports this quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家预计本季度出口会小幅下降。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to look out for, so the modern verb is that watch turned into a claim about the future.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「向外张望」，因此现代动词就是那种张望变成了对未来的断言。

senses.title: Await an arrival
senses.definition: to be waiting for a person or thing that is due to come
senses.definitionCN: 正在等候按计划要来的人或物
senses.example: We expect the auditors at nine and the courier before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们等审计人员九点到，快递中午前到。
senses.why: Waiting is the original physical sense, and it survives whenever the object is a person or a delivery rather than a fact.
senses.whyCN: 等待是最初的具体义，只要对象是人或送来的东西而非事实，它就仍然成立。

senses.title: Require as a duty
senses.definition: to require something of someone because a rule, role or standard demands it
senses.definitionCN: 因规则、身份或标准而要求某人做到某事
senses.example: The school expects students to cite every source.
senses.exampleCN: 学校要求学生为每一处来源标注出处。
senses.why: A prediction about a person's behaviour easily becomes an obligation, which is how the demanding sense grew out of the forecasting one.
senses.whyCN: 对人的行为所作预判很容易变成义务，要求的义项就是这样从预判义长出来的。

senses.title: Suppose without certainty
senses.definition: to suppose or guess, often marked as uncertain in speech
senses.definitionCN: 推测或猜想，口语中常带不确定的标记
senses.example: I expect you have already heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜你已经听说这个消息了。
senses.why: When the evidence is thin, the same verb softens into mere supposition, and English marks this with a plain declarative tone.
senses.whyCN: 证据不足时，同一个动词软化为单纯的推测，英语靠平直的陈述语气来标出这一点。

senses.title: Be expecting a baby
senses.definition: in the progressive, to be pregnant
senses.definitionCN: 用于进行时，指正在怀孕
senses.example: She is expecting in early spring and has already told her team.
senses.exampleCN: 她初春就要生产，已经告诉了团队。
senses.why: The waiting sense is applied to a birth, and English uses the progressive as a polite stand-in for the word pregnant.
senses.whyCN: 等待义被用到生产上，英语用进行时作为「怀孕」的委婉说法。

senses.title: Forecast in figures
senses.definition: to forecast a quantity, as analysts do with prices, demand or earnings
senses.definitionCN: 像分析师对价格、需求或收益那样预测一个数量
senses.example: Analysts expect inflation to stay above target until winter.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师预计通胀会一直高于目标直到冬季。
senses.why: Once the object is a number, the verb belongs to forecasting, and the sentence reads as a projection rather than a hope.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对象是数字，这个动词就属于预测语境，句子读起来是投影而非愿望。

senses.title: Require much of someone
senses.definition: to demand a high level of effort or behaviour from someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的努力或表现提出很高要求
senses.example: The coach expects a great deal from the senior rowers.
senses.exampleCN: 教练对资深桨手要求很高。
senses.why: The demanding sense intensifies when the standard is high, and the verb then describes pressure rather than prediction.
senses.whyCN: 标准一高，要求的义项就加重，这个动词于是描述压力而不是预判。

senses.title: Be due to arrive
senses.definition: to be scheduled or due, as a train or flight is
senses.definitionCN: 如列车或航班那样，按安排应当到达
senses.example: The flight is expected at half past six, weather permitting.
senses.exampleCN: 天气允许的话，这班飞机预计六点半到。
senses.why: Schedules turned the verb into a passive formula, which is why stations and airports use it for anything with a timetable.
senses.whyCN: 时刻表把这个动词变成了被动套语，因此车站与机场用它指任何有时间表的事物。

intro.en: Expect comes from Latin exspectare 'to look out for', a prefix meaning 'out' plus a frequentative verb for looking. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expect 来自拉丁语 exspectare「向外张望」，由表「向外」的前缀加一个表示反复看的动词构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix meant 'out, outward', aiming the gaze beyond the present spot.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为「向外、出去」，把目光投向当下位置之外。

items.en: Spectare 'to look at' was built on the verb for seeing; the deeper origin of that verb is not established.
items.cn: spectare「看」建立在表「看见」的动词上；那个动词的更早来源未得到证明。

items.en: The compound meant 'to look out for, await', and it already carried both the watching and the believing.
items.cn: 这个复合动词意为「向外张望、等待」，已经同时带着「看」与「相信」。

items.en: The verb reached English in the fourteenth century, and the sense of requiring something of a person appears by the sixteenth.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪进入英语，而「对人提出要求」的义项到十六世纪才出现。

items.en: Timetables gave the passive formula for arrivals, and the progressive became a standard way to say that someone is pregnant.
items.cn: 时刻表给出了关于到达的被动套语，进行时则成为说某人怀孕的常用方式。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest English use is recorded only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of the verb for seeing is unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：最早的英语用例只有约略记载；那个表「看见」的动词在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words and the near look-alike that share the looking verb; group two holds near neighbours for waiting and for requiring.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词以及共用「看」这一动词的近形词；第二组是表示等待与要求的近义词。

entries.definition: The noun for the belief or the standard; the verb needs a subject and a clause where the noun needs only a possessive.
entries.definitionCN: 指信念或标准的名词；动词需要主语与从句，而名词只需所有格。

entries.definition: An adjective describing someone already in a waiting state; the verb describes the act of forecasting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容已处在等待状态的人；动词描述的是预判这一行为。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning 'in, into' plus the same looking root, so it means examining closely, not awaiting.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「向内」的前缀加同一个「看」词根构成，意为仔细检查而非等待。

entries.definition: Built with a prefix meaning 'back' plus the same root, so it originally meant looking back with regard; it has no forecasting sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「向后」的前缀加同一词根构成，原指回头看重，并无预判义。

entries.definition: To expect something and often to act in advance because of it; the English verb stresses the preparation, not the belief.
entries.definitionCN: 指预料某事，且常因此提前行动；这个英语动词强调准备而非信念。

entries.definition: A formal verb for waiting on a person or event; it carries no forecasting claim about whether the thing will come.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指等候某人或某事；它并不断言那件事是否真会来。

entries.definition: To assume something for the sake of argument or in the absence of proof; expect is usually stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 指为讨论起见或在无证据时假定某事；expect 通常更强。

entries.definition: To demand something as necessary, often with authority; expect only implies a demand when context supplies the authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指凭借权威要求某事为必需；expect 只有在语境给出权威时才含要求。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real looking root, the real family and the real patterns.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、表「看」的词根、真实的词族与真实的句式。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to look out for, so expecting is keeping watch in advance.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为「向外张望」，因此期待就是提前守住目光。

normal.en: The looking root also builds spectator, inspect, respect and spectacle.
normal.cn: 表「看」的词根还构成 spectator、inspect、respect 与 spectacle。

normal.en: The family runs expect, expected, unexpected, expectant, expectation, expectancy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 expect、expected、unexpected、expectant、expectation、expectancy。

normal.en: The common patterns are expect to do and expect somebody to do.
normal.cn: 常见句式是「预计做某事」与「指望某人做某事」。

normal.en: The progressive be expecting is the polite way to say pregnant.
normal.cn: 进行时说法是「怀孕」的委婉表达。

abstract.en: Picture a hand already on the door handle before the knock comes.
abstract.cn: 想象敲门声还没响，手已经握在门把上。

abstract.en: Picture a timetable that announces a train nobody can see yet.
abstract.cn: 想象时刻表宣布一班还看不见的列车。

abstract.en: Picture a teacher who writes the standard on the board before the work starts.
abstract.cn: 想象老师在开工前先把标准写在黑板上。

examples.en: We expect the results by Friday, though the lab has not promised anything.
examples.cn: 我们预计周五前出结果，尽管实验室并未承诺。

examples.en: She expects her students to question every figure they are given.
examples.cn: 她要求学生质疑给到他们的每一个数字。

examples.en: The concert is expected to start twenty minutes late.
examples.cn: 音乐会预计晚二十分钟开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外看」——把目光提前投出去等结果，就是期待与预计

root: 拉丁 exspectare「向外张望」由意为「向外」的前缀加 spectare（反复看）；spectare 出自表「看见」的词根，该词根更深来源不确定。英语 expect。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one watch: looking out for what is coming. The watch becomes a forecast, then a wait, then a rule imposed on someone, then a bare guess, then a pregnancy, then a projection in figures, then a high demand, and finally a line on a timetable.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一道目光展开：向外张望将要到来之物。这道目光依次变成预判、等候、加于他人的规矩、纯然的猜测、怀孕、以数字作出的投影、很高的要求，最后是时刻表上的一行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a doorway looking outward with a hand already on the handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在门口向外望，手已经握在门把上。

branches.en: FORECAST: a plain belief about the future and a projection in figures are the same claim at different precision.
branches.cn: 预判：对未来的朴素信念与以数字作出的投影，是同一断言的不同精度。

branches.en: WAITING: awaiting a guest and a flight due on a timetable are the watch made concrete.
branches.cn: 等待：等客人，与等时刻表上的航班，都是那道目光的具体化。

branches.en: DEMAND: a rule imposed on someone and a high standard set for them are expectation turned into pressure.
branches.cn: 要求：加于人的规矩与为人设下的高标准，都是预期变成了压力。

branches.en: BARE GUESS: when evidence thins, the same verb softens into supposition.
branches.cn: 纯然猜测：证据变薄时，同一个动词软化为推测。

branches.en: WAITING FOR A BIRTH: the polite progressive borrows the waiting sense for pregnancy.
branches.cn: 等待生产：委婉的进行时把等待义借去指怀孕。

intro.en: Expect is a short Latin verb of two pieces, and both pieces build large English families.
intro.cn: expect 是一个由两部分构成的简短拉丁动词，两部分都构成大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix meaning 'out' gives export, exclude and extend; the looking root gives inspect, respect, spectator and spectacle.
latinIntro.cn: 表「向外」的前缀衍生 export、exclude 与 extend；表「看」的词根衍生 inspect、respect、spectator 与 spectacle。

items.example: The prefix aims the looking beyond the present place.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把目光投向当下所在之外。

items.example: The root supplies the watching that the word is built on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供这个词所由建立的「看」。

items.example: The verb keeps the prefix and drops the repeated-looking suffix.
items.exampleCN: 动词保留前缀，去掉了表反复看的那层后缀。

items.example: The suffix builds the noun of the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出该行为的名词。

items.example: The noun is far more common than a literal translation suggests.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词远比字面直译看来常用。

items.example: The suffix builds the adjective for someone waiting.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出形容等待者的形容词。

items.meaning: waiting; about to become a parent
items.meaningCN: 期待着的；即将为人父母的
items.example: The adjective has a settled medical use.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词有固定的医疗用法。

items.example: The participle form builds the ordinary adjective of scheduled things.
items.exampleCN: 分词形式造出指按计划之事的常用形容词。

items.meaningCN: 按计划发生的；被预见的
items.example: The adjective appears in timetables and in test marking.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词出现在时刻表与阅卷语境中。

items.example: The negative prefix marks what no forecast covered.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀标出预判未覆盖之事。

definition_zh: 餐馆；饭店
definition_en: a place where you pay to sit and eat meals
core_image: 一间亮着灯的店，里面摆着桌椅和热腾腾的饭菜
scene: 我们在一家小餐馆吃了热汤面。 We had hot noodle soup at a small restaurant.
sceneCN: 这里 restaurant 是「餐馆」（第 1 个义项：供人付费用餐的场所）；句意：我们在一家小餐馆吃了热汤面。

derivatives.zh: 餐馆经营者
常去餐馆的人

senses.title: A place serving meals
senses.definition: a place where meals are cooked and served to paying customers
senses.definitionCN: 为付费顾客烹饪并提供饭菜的场所
senses.example: We found a quiet restaurant near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近找到一家安静的餐馆。
senses.why: French restaurant originally named a restoring broth, then the place that served it.
senses.whyCN: 法语 restaurant 最初指一种恢复体力的汤，后来指供应这种汤的地方。

senses.title: The business itself
senses.definition: the business or organization that runs such a place
senses.definitionCN: 经营这类场所的生意或组织
senses.example: The restaurant employs forty people.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐馆雇用了四十人。
senses.why: A restaurant can be spoken of as a business, not only as a building.
senses.whyCN: 餐馆不仅可以指建筑，也可以作为生意来谈论。

intro.en: Restaurant comes from French restaurer, to restore, because the first restaurants served a broth believed to restore health.
intro.cn: restaurant 来自法语 restaurer（恢复），因为最早的餐馆供应一种被认为能恢复健康的汤。

items.en: Restaurare means to restore or rebuild.
items.cn: restaurare 意为恢复、重建。

items.en: Restaurer means to restore.
items.cn: restaurer 意为恢复。

items.en: Restaurant first names a restoring broth.
items.cn: restaurant 最初指一种恢复体力的汤。

items.en: The word shifts to the place that serves food.
items.cn: 这个词转为指供应食物的场所。

items.en: English restaurant names a dining place.
items.cn: 英语 restaurant 指用餐场所。

items.en: Modern English uses it for all kinds of dining businesses.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指各类餐饮生意。

note.en: Restaurant is a dining-place word, close to its French-derived relatives and to other eating places.
note.cn: restaurant 是表示用餐场所的词，与法语来源的亲属词以及其他餐饮场所词相邻。

entries.definition: a restaurant owner
entries.definitionCN: 餐馆经营者

entries.definition: a person who often eats out
entries.definitionCN: 常去餐馆的人

entries.definition: to restore or relax
entries.definitionCN: 恢复；休息

entries.definition: a small place serving drinks and light meals
entries.definitionCN: 咖啡馆；小餐馆

entries.definition: a cheap informal restaurant
entries.definitionCN: 小餐馆；餐车式饭馆

entries.definition: an informal word for a restaurant
entries.definitionCN: 餐馆（口语）

normalIntro.en: Restaurant began as a restoring broth: food that puts strength back into you.
normalIntro.cn: restaurant 最初是一种「恢复体力」的汤：让你重新有力气的食物。

normal.en: A restaurant serves meals for payment.
normal.cn: restaurant 为付费顾客提供饭菜。

normal.en: A restaurant owner is a restaurateur.
normal.cn: 餐馆老板是 restaurateur。

normal.en: A restaurant chain runs many branches.
normal.cn: restaurant chain 经营许多分店。

normal.en: Fast-food restaurants serve food quickly.
normal.cn: fast-food restaurant 快速供应食物。

normal.en: Compare café: a café is smaller and often serves drinks.
normal.cn: 对比 café：café 更小，常供应饮品。

abstract.en: Picture a warm window with tables and lamps inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇温暖的窗，里面摆着桌子和灯。

abstract.en: Imagine steam rising from a bowl of soup.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗汤冒着热气。

abstract.en: Think of a waiter carrying plates between tables.
abstract.cn: 想象服务员在桌间端着盘子穿行。

examples.en: The restaurant was full by seven o'clock.
examples.cn: 七点时餐馆已经坐满了。

examples.en: He works as a cook in a French restaurant.
examples.cn: 他在一家法国餐馆当厨师。

examples.en: They opened a second restaurant last spring.
examples.cn: 他们去年春天开了第二家餐馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rest + aurant」——进去「歇一歇」再吃顿饭，就是餐馆；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 restaurare（恢复）→ 法语 restaurer → restaurant（恢复体力的汤，后指供应食物的场所）→ 英语 restaurant，核心义「让人恢复精神的用餐处」。

sensesIntro.en: Restaurant first means the place that serves meals, and then the business that operates it.
sensesIntro.cn: restaurant 先指供应饭菜的场所，再指经营它的生意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room where hot food restores tired people.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间亮着灯的房间，热饭让疲惫的人恢复精神。

branches.en: The dining place is the everyday sense.
The business sense treats it as an enterprise.
branches.cn: 生意义项把它视为企业。

branches.en: A restaurant is both a room and a company.
branches.cn: 餐馆既是空间也是公司。

branches.en: A café, a diner, and a canteen can all be restaurants.
branches.cn: 咖啡馆、小饭馆与食堂都可以是餐馆。

branches.en: Chains and family restaurants differ in size, not in kind.
branches.cn: 连锁店与家庭餐馆规模不同，性质相同。

intro.en: Restaurant is a French restoring word, with English relatives restaurateur and restaurant-goer.
intro.cn: restaurant 是法语中表示「恢复」的词，英语亲属有 restaurateur 与 restaurant-goer。

latinIntro.en: Latin restaurare means to restore, and French restaurer keeps that sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 restaurare 意为恢复，法语 restaurer 保留这一含义。

items.example: Restaurer carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: restaurer 把这个词带入法语。
restaurant-goer 在 restaurant 后加 goer。
